   171→/// Delegation template for a specific role (role-agnostic design)
   172→///
   173→/// Roles like "customer", "admin", "node" are just labels that map to
   174→/// different capability and pattern sets. The protocol only sees capabilities.
   175→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   176→pub struct DelegationTemplate {
   177→    /// Token type for delegated token (e.g., "page_viewer", "page_share")
   178→    pub token_type: String,
   179→    /// Explicit protocol capabilities (relay, share, accept_publish)
   180→    #[serde(default)]
   181→    pub peer_capabilities: PeerCapabilities,
   182→    /// Operations that this role can perform (e.g., "add_pages", "share_page")
   183→    /// operation_name -> "allow" | "deny"
   184→    #[serde(default)]
   185→    pub operations: HashMap<String, String>,
   186→    /// Auth capabilities (can_connect, sync_enabled, etc.)
   187→    #[serde(default)]
   188→    pub auth_capabilities: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
   189→    /// Layer patterns with placeholders like {page_id}, {aud}
   190→    /// Pattern -> { create: bool, sync: bool }
   191→    #[serde(default)]
   192→    pub layer_patterns: HashMap<String, LayerPatternConfig>,
   193→    /// Fixed layers (non-pattern) with their capabilities
   194→    /// layer_name -> { capability: "viewer"|"collaborator", sync: bool }
   195→    #[serde(default)]
   196→    pub layers: HashMap<String, LayerConfig>,
   197→    /// Relationship label (for logging/debugging only, NOT for business logic)
   198→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   199→    pub relationship: Option<String>,
   200→    /// Self-describing templates: what to issue when holder takes actions
   201→    /// Keys: "page_request", "share_link", etc.
   202→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty")]
   203→    pub issue_on: HashMap<String, Box<DelegationTemplate>>,
   204→    /// Presence configuration (visibility, display name)
   205→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   206→    pub presence: Option<PresenceConfig>,
   207→    /// Allowed ephemeral function names (empty = all allowed)
   208→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
   209→    pub ephemeral_funcs: Vec<String>,
   210→    /// Schemas for dynamically-created layers (channels, DMs, orders)
   211→    /// Key is the pattern template (e.g., "channels/{id}/messages")
   212→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty")]
   213→    pub dynamic_layer_schemas: HashMap<String, DynamicLayerSchema>,
   214→    /// Explicit layer recipients for layer authority issuance.
   215→    ///
   216→    /// Omitted => role-based distribution
   217→    /// [did...] => explicit distribution
   218→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   219→    pub authorized_peers: Option<Vec<String>>,
   220→}

   222→/// Configuration for a fixed (non-pattern) layer
   223→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   224→pub struct LayerConfig {
   225→    /// Whether to sync this layer
   226→    #[serde(default)]
   227→    pub sync: bool,
   228→    /// Whether holder can write to this layer
   229→    #[serde(default)]
   230→    pub write: bool,
   231→    /// Layer type: "list", "map", "text"
   232→    #[serde(rename = "type", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]

   236→/// Schema for dynamically-created layers (channels, DMs, orders)
   237→///
   238→/// Dynamic layers are created at runtime and granted via permit re-issuance.
   239→/// The schema defines what types of dynamic layers an app supports.
   240→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   241→pub struct DynamicLayerSchema {
   242→    /// Layer type: "map", "list", "text"
   243→    #[serde(rename = "type", default)]
   244→    pub layer_type: String,
   245→    /// Grant type: "role" (all peers) or "explicit" (named participants)
   246→    #[serde(default)]
   247→    pub grant: GrantType,
   248→    /// Permissions per role (for role-granted schemas)
   249→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty")]
   250→    pub role_permissions: HashMap<String, LayerConfig>,
   251→    /// Permissions for explicit grants
   252→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   253→    pub permissions: Option<LayerConfig>,
   254→}
   255→
   256→/// How a dynamic layer is granted to peers
   257→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, PartialEq)]
   258→#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
   259→pub enum GrantType {
   260→    /// Granted to all peers of matching roles
   261→    #[default]
   262→    Role,
   263→    /// Granted only to explicitly named participants
   264→    Explicit,

   267→/// Presence configuration for a peer
   268→///
   269→/// Controls visibility in the /users layer and presence events.
   270→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   271→pub struct PresenceConfig {
   272→    /// Whether this peer is visible to others (presence layer entry written)
   273→    #[serde(default)]
   274→    pub visible: bool,
   275→    /// Whether this peer can see others' presence (receives presence layer sync)
   276→    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
   277→    pub can_see_others: bool,

   279→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   280→    pub name: Option<String>,

   287→/// Internal struct for deserializing permit facts via serde
   288→///
   289→/// This replaces ~80 lines of manual JSON extraction with a single deserialize call.
   290→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
   291→struct PermitFacts {
   292→    #[serde(default)]
   293→    peer_capabilities: PeerCapabilities,
   294→    #[serde(default)]
   295→    layer_patterns: HashMap<String, LayerPatternConfig>,
   296→    #[serde(default)]
   297→    layers: HashMap<String, LayerConfig>,
   298→    #[serde(default)]
   299→    issue_on: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
   300→    /// Sync behavior facts (local_only, no_incoming_updates, send_full_snapshot)
   301→    #[serde(default)]
   302→    sync: SyncFacts,
   303→    /// Presence configuration (visibility, display name)
   304→    #[serde(default)]
   305→    presence: Option<PresenceConfig>,
   306→    /// Allowed ephemeral function names (empty = all allowed)
   307→    #[serde(default)]
   308→    ephemeral_funcs: Vec<String>,
   309→    /// Schemas for dynamically-created layers
   310→    #[serde(default)]
   311→    dynamic_layer_schemas: HashMap<String, DynamicLayerSchema>,

   313→
   314→impl DelegationTemplate {
   315→    /// Convert template to permit facts JSON
   316→    ///
   317→    /// This creates the facts structure that will be embedded in the delegated token.
   318→    /// Role-agnostic: only includes capabilities and patterns, no role-based logic.
   319→    pub fn to_facts(&self) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {
   320→        let mut facts = serde_json::Map::new();
   321→
   322→        // Add token_type
   323→        facts.insert(
   324→            "token_type".to_string(),
   325→            serde_json::Value::String(self.token_type.clone()),
   326→        );
   327→
   328→        // Add peer_capabilities
   329→        facts.insert(
   330→            "peer_capabilities".to_string(),
   331→            self.peer_capabilities.to_json(),
   332→        );
   333→
   334→        // Add operations (required for delegation chain - e.g., add_pages permission)
   335→        if !self.operations.is_empty() {
   336→            let ops_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   337→                .operations
   338→                .iter()
   339→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), serde_json::Value::String(v.clone())))
   340→                .collect();
   341→            facts.insert(
   342→                "operations".to_string(),
   343→                serde_json::Value::Object(ops_json),
   344→            );
   345→        }
   346→
   347→        // Add auth_capabilities
   348→        if !self.auth_capabilities.is_empty() {
   349→            let auth_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   350→                .auth_capabilities
   351→                .iter()
   352→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   353→                .collect();
   354→            facts.insert(
   355→                "auth_capabilities".to_string(),
   356→                serde_json::Value::Object(auth_json),
   357→            );
   358→        }
   359→
   360→        // Add layer_patterns
   361→        if !self.layer_patterns.is_empty() {
   362→            let patterns_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   363→                .layer_patterns
   364→                .iter()
   365→                .map(|(pattern, config)| {
   366→                    (
   367→                        pattern.clone(),
   368→                        serde_json::json!({
   369→                            "create": config.create,
   370→                            "sync": config.sync,
   371→                            "write": config.write
   372→                        }),
   373→                    )
   374→                })
   375→                .collect();
   376→            facts.insert(
   377→                "layer_patterns".to_string(),
   378→                serde_json::Value::Object(patterns_json),
   379→            );
   380→        }
   381→
   382→        // Add fixed layers
   383→        if !self.layers.is_empty() {
   384→            let layers_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   385→                .layers
   386→                .iter()
   387→                .map(|(name, config)| {
   388→                    let mut layer_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
   389→                    layer_obj.insert("sync".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.sync));
   390→                    layer_obj.insert("write".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.write));
   391→                    if let Some(ref t) = config.layer_type {
   392→                        layer_obj.insert("type".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(t.clone()));
   393→                    }
   394→                    (name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(layer_obj))
   395→                })
   396→                .collect();
   397→            facts.insert("layers".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(layers_json));
   398→        }
   399→
   400→        // Add relationship (for logging only)
   401→        if let Some(rel) = &self.relationship {
   402→            facts.insert(
   403→                "relationship".to_string(),
   404→                serde_json::Value::String(rel.clone()),
   405→            );
   406→        }
   407→
   408→        // Add issue_on (self-describing templates for what to issue on actions)
   409→        if !self.issue_on.is_empty() {
   410→            let issue_on_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   411→                .issue_on
   412→                .iter()
   413→                .map(|(action, template)| {
   414→                    (
   415→                        action.clone(),
   416→                        serde_json::Value::Object(template.to_facts()),
   417→                    )
   418→                })
   419→                .collect();
   420→            facts.insert(
   421→                "issue_on".to_string(),
   422→                serde_json::Value::Object(issue_on_json),
   423→            );
   424→        }
   425→
   426→        // Add presence configuration
   427→        if let Some(ref presence) = self.presence {
   428→            let mut presence_json = serde_json::Map::new();
   429→            presence_json.insert(
   430→                "visible".to_string(),
   431→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.visible),
   432→            );
   433→            presence_json.insert(
   434→                "can_see_others".to_string(),
   435→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.can_see_others),
   436→            );
   437→            if let Some(ref name) = presence.name {
   438→                presence_json.insert("name".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(name.clone()));
   439→            }
   440→            facts.insert(
   441→                "presence".to_string(),
   442→                serde_json::Value::Object(presence_json),
   443→            );
   444→        }
   445→
   446→        // Add ephemeral_funcs (allowed ephemeral function names)
   447→        if !self.ephemeral_funcs.is_empty() {
   448→            let funcs: Vec<serde_json::Value> = self
   449→                .ephemeral_funcs
   450→                .iter()
   451→                .map(|f| serde_json::Value::String(f.clone()))
   452→                .collect();
   453→            facts.insert(
   454→                "ephemeral_funcs".to_string(),
   455→                serde_json::Value::Array(funcs),
   456→            );
   457→        }
   458→
   459→        // Add dynamic_layer_schemas
   460→        if !self.dynamic_layer_schemas.is_empty() {
   461→            let schemas_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   462→                .dynamic_layer_schemas
   463→                .iter()
   464→                .map(|(pattern, schema)| {
   465→                    (
   466→                        pattern.clone(),
   467→                        serde_json::to_value(schema).unwrap_or_default(),
   468→                    )
   469→                })
   470→                .collect();
   471→            facts.insert(
   472→                "dynamic_layer_schemas".to_string(),
   473→                serde_json::Value::Object(schemas_json),
   474→            );
   475→        }
   476→
   477→        // Add authorized_peers for layer authority templates.
   478→        // Missing/None means role-based distribution.
   479→        if self.token_type == "layer_authority" {
   480→            if let Some(peers) = &self.authorized_peers {
   481→                let values = peers
   482→                    .iter()
   483→                    .map(|did| serde_json::Value::String(did.clone()))
   484→                    .collect();
   485→                facts.insert(
   486→                    "authorized_peers".to_string(),
   487→                    serde_json::Value::Array(values),
   488→                );
   489→            }
   490→        }
   491→
   492→        facts
   493→    }
   494→}

   496→/// Parsed Permit token with domain logic (role-agnostic design).
   497→///
   498→/// The protocol only sees capabilities and patterns, not role labels.
   499→/// Contains all permit data including raw token, parsed UCAN, and extracted facts.
   500→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   501→pub struct Permit {
   502→    // Core permit data (merged from PermitCore)
   503→    /// Raw permit token string
   504→    raw_token: String,
   505→    /// Parsed token (uses ucan library internally)
   506→    parsed: Ucan,
   507→    /// Raw facts as JSON (source of truth)
   508→    facts: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
   509→
   510→    // Extracted/parsed fields
   511→    /// Explicit protocol capabilities (relay, share, accept_publish)
   512→    peer_capabilities: PeerCapabilities,
   513→    /// Fixed layer configs (layer_name -> config)
   514→    layers: HashMap<String, LayerConfig>,
   515→    /// Layer patterns for identity-based access (pattern -> config)
   516→    /// Patterns support `{aud}`, `{page_id}` placeholders
   517→    layer_patterns: HashMap<String, LayerPatternConfig>,
   518→    /// Self-describing templates: what to issue when holder takes actions
   519→    /// Keys: "page_request", "share_link", etc.
   520→    issue_on: HashMap<String, DelegationTemplate>,
   521→    /// Parent permit CIDs for delegation chain
   522→    proof_chain: Vec<String>,
   523→    /// Sync behavior facts (local_only, no_incoming_updates, send_full_snapshot)
   524→    sync_facts: SyncFacts,
   525→    /// Presence configuration (visibility, display name)
   526→    presence: Option<PresenceConfig>,
   527→    /// Allowed ephemeral function names (empty = all allowed)
   528→    ephemeral_funcs: Vec<String>,
   529→    /// Schemas for dynamically-created layers (channels, DMs, orders)
   530→    dynamic_layer_schemas: HashMap<String, DynamicLayerSchema>,
   531→}
   532→
   533→impl Permit {
   534→    /// Parse permit token and extract all domain information.
   535→    ///
   536→    /// Role-agnostic: extracts capabilities and patterns, not role labels.
   537→    pub fn from_token(token: &str) -> PermitResult<Self> {
   538→        use tracing::trace;
   539→
   540→        trace!("Parsing permit token (len={})", token.len());
   541→
   542→        // Parse permit token (uses ucan library internally)
   543→        let parsed = Ucan::try_from(token)
   544→            .map_err(|e| PermitError::ParsingFailed(format!("Permit parsing error: {}", e)))?;
   545→
   546→        trace!(
   547→            "JWT decoded - issuer: {}, audience: {}",
   548→            parsed.issuer(),
   549→            parsed.audience()
   550→        );
   551→
   552→        // Extract facts as raw JSON (source of truth)
   553→        let facts_ref = parsed
   554→            .facts()
   555→            .as_ref()
   556→            .ok_or_else(|| PermitError::MissingField("Permit facts not found".to_string()))?;
   557→
   558→        // Convert BTreeMap to serde_json::Value for deserialization
   559→        let facts_value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(facts_ref)
   560→            .map_err(|e| PermitError::ParsingFailed(format!("Facts conversion error: {}", e)))?;
   561→
   562→        // Deserialize structured facts via serde (replaces ~60 lines of manual parsing)
   563→        let parsed_facts: PermitFacts =
   564→            serde_json::from_value(facts_value.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
   565→
   566→        // Keep raw facts map for get_fact() lookups
   567→        let facts: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = facts_ref
   568→            .iter()
   569→            .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   570→            .collect();
   571→
   572→        trace!(facts = ?facts.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(), "Facts extracted");
   573→
   574→        // Parse issue_on templates
   575→        let issue_on: HashMap<String, DelegationTemplate> = parsed_facts
   576→            .issue_on
   577→            .iter()
   578→            .filter_map(|(key, val)| {
   579→                Self::parse_delegation_template(key, val).map(|t| (key.clone(), t))
   580→            })
   581→            .collect();
   582→
   583→        // Extract proof chain
   584→        let proof_chain = parsed.proofs().clone().unwrap_or_default();
   585→
   586→        Ok(Self {
   587→            raw_token: token.to_string(),
   588→            parsed,
   589→            facts,
   590→            peer_capabilities: parsed_facts.peer_capabilities,
   591→            layers: parsed_facts.layers,
   592→            layer_patterns: parsed_facts.layer_patterns,
   593→            issue_on,
   594→            proof_chain,
   595→            sync_facts: parsed_facts.sync,
   596→            presence: parsed_facts.presence,
   597→            ephemeral_funcs: parsed_facts.ephemeral_funcs,
   598→            dynamic_layer_schemas: parsed_facts.dynamic_layer_schemas,
   599→        })
   600→    }

   602→    /// Parse a DelegationTemplate from a JSON value
   603→    fn parse_delegation_template(
   604→        key: &str,
   605→        template_val: &serde_json::Value,
   606→    ) -> Option<DelegationTemplate> {
   607→        let template_obj = template_val.as_object()?;
   608→
   609→        // Extract token_type
   610→        let token_type = template_obj
   611→            .get("token_type")
   612→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   613→            .map(String::from)
   614→            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("delegated_{}", key));
   615→
   616→        // Extract peer_capabilities
   617→        let peer_capabilities = template_obj
   618→            .get("peer_capabilities")
   619→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   620→            .map(PeerCapabilities::from_json)
   621→            .unwrap_or_default();
   622→
   623→        // Extract layer_patterns
   624→        let mut layer_patterns = HashMap::new();
   625→        if let Some(patterns_obj) = template_obj
   626→            .get("layer_patterns")
   627→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   628→        {
   629→            for (pattern, config) in patterns_obj {
   630→                if let Some(config_obj) = config.as_object() {
   631→                    layer_patterns.insert(
   632→                        pattern.clone(),
   633→                        LayerPatternConfig {
   634→                            create: config_obj
   635→                                .get("create")
   636→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   637→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   638→                            sync: config_obj
   639→                                .get("sync")
   640→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   641→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   642→                            write: config_obj
   643→                                .get("write")
   644→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   645→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   646→                        },
   647→                    );
   648→                }
   649→            }
   650→        }
   651→
   652→        // Extract fixed layers
   653→        let mut layers = HashMap::new();
   654→        if let Some(layers_obj) = template_obj.get("layers").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   655→            for (layer_name, layer_val) in layers_obj {
   656→                if let Some(layer_obj) = layer_val.as_object() {
   657→                    layers.insert(
   658→                        layer_name.clone(),
   659→                        LayerConfig {
   660→                            sync: layer_obj
   661→                                .get("sync")
   662→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   663→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   664→                            write: layer_obj
   665→                                .get("write")
   666→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   667→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   668→                            layer_type: layer_obj
   669→                                .get("type")
   670→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   671→                                .map(String::from),
   672→                        },
   673→                    );
   674→                }
   675→            }
   676→        }
   677→
   678→        // Extract relationship (for logging only)
   679→        let relationship = template_obj
   680→            .get("relationship")
   681→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   682→            .map(String::from);
   683→
   684→        // Extract operations (e.g., add_pages, share_page)
   685→        let mut operations = HashMap::new();
   686→        if let Some(ops_obj) = template_obj.get("operations").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   687→            for (op_name, op_val) in ops_obj {
   688→                if let Some(op_str) = op_val.as_str() {
   689→                    operations.insert(op_name.clone(), op_str.to_string());
   690→                }
   691→            }
   692→        }
   693→
   694→        // Extract auth_capabilities (can_connect, sync_enabled, etc.)
   695→        let mut auth_capabilities = HashMap::new();
   696→        if let Some(auth_obj) = template_obj
   697→            .get("auth_capabilities")
   698→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   699→        {
   700→            for (cap_name, cap_val) in auth_obj {
   701→                auth_capabilities.insert(cap_name.clone(), cap_val.clone());
   702→            }
   703→        }
   704→
   705→        // Extract issue_on (recursive - templates for what to issue on actions)
   706→        let mut issue_on = HashMap::new();
   707→        if let Some(issue_on_obj) = template_obj.get("issue_on").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   708→            for (action_key, nested_template_val) in issue_on_obj {
   709→                if let Some(nested_template) =
   710→                    Self::parse_delegation_template(action_key, nested_template_val)
   711→                {
   712→                    issue_on.insert(action_key.clone(), Box::new(nested_template));
   713→                }
   714→            }
   715→        }
   716→
   717→        // Extract presence configuration
   718→        let presence = template_obj
   719→            .get("presence")
   720→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   721→            .map(|p| PresenceConfig {
   722→                visible: p.get("visible").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
   723→                can_see_others: p
   724→                    .get("can_see_others")
   725→                    .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   726→                    .unwrap_or(true),
   727→                name: p.get("name").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(String::from),
   728→            });
   729→
   730→        // Extract ephemeral_funcs
   731→        let ephemeral_funcs = template_obj
   732→            .get("ephemeral_funcs")
   733→            .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
   734→            .map(|arr| {
   735→                arr.iter()
   736→                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))
   737→                    .collect()
   738→            })
   739→            .unwrap_or_default();
   740→
   741→        // Extract dynamic_layer_schemas
   742→        let mut dynamic_layer_schemas = HashMap::new();
   743→        if let Some(schemas_obj) = template_obj
   744→            .get("dynamic_layer_schemas")
   745→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   746→        {
   747→            for (pattern, schema_val) in schemas_obj {
   748→                if let Ok(schema) = serde_json::from_value::<DynamicLayerSchema>(schema_val.clone())
   749→                {
   750→                    dynamic_layer_schemas.insert(pattern.clone(), schema);
   751→                }
   752→            }
   753→        }
   754→
   755→        let authorized_peers = parse_authorized_peers_fact(template_obj.get("authorized_peers"))
   756→            .ok()
   757→            .flatten();
   758→
   759→        Some(DelegationTemplate {
   760→            token_type,
   761→            peer_capabilities,
   762→            operations,
   763→            auth_capabilities,
   764→            layer_patterns,
   765→            layers,
   766→            relationship,
   767→            issue_on,
   768→            presence,
   769→            ephemeral_funcs,
   770→            dynamic_layer_schemas,
   771→            authorized_peers,
   772→        })
   773→    }

The plan is written at `docs/PLAN_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE.md`. Here's a summary of what it covers:

**The core shift**: From monolith page permits with role-based access to per-layer permits with capabilities. The permit_template goes from 957 lines to ~40 lines.

**5 implementation phases**:

| Phase | What | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1 | Rich LayerUnit (self-contained with subscribers, VVs, broadcast) | scribe only |
| 2 | Per-layer permits + capabilities (replace roles) | gurkha + scribe |
| 3 | Unified wire protocol (LayerSync + LayerConsent) | courier + scribe |
| 4 | Butler storage + cold/warm lifecycle | butler + scribe |
| 5 | page_id transparency + cleanup | all crates + apps |

Each phase is independently valuable and testable. Phase 1 is purely internal to scribe with no external API changes — safest to start with.

Key design decisions captured:
- **Layer permit** (node → viewer) = "you can write to this layer on my system"
- **Layer consent** (viewer → node) = "you can push updates to my local data"
- **Dynamic grant types**: `open` (everyone gets a permit) replaces `role` with all roles listed. `explicit` stays for DMs.
- **sync_target rule**: the one special case — viewer always pushes to node without permit
- **No `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber`**, no `pending_layer_authorizations`, no `authorized_dids` HashSet

1→# Plan: Layer-Centric Architecture
     2→
     3→## Problem Statement
     4→
     5→The current authorization system has three fundamental issues:
     6→
     7→1. **Monolith page permits** — A single page permit lists every layer, every role's permissions, nested `issue_on` delegation chains, and `dynamic_layer_schemas`. The permit_template.json is 957 lines with 6+ copies of the same layer block. Installing a new app requires reissuing every peer's page permit.
     8→
     9→2. **Role-based access** — Authorization is tied to role names ("owner", "collaborator", "viewer", "node"). Code checks `allowed_roles.contains(role)` and `role_permissions.get(role)`. This prevents fine-grained capability control.
    10→
    11→3. **Eager authorization cache** — `authorized_dids: HashSet<String>` on each LayerUnit is populated from 11+ disconnected call sites, causing race conditions, bugs (viewer writes to dynamic channels fail), and a complex wire protocol chain just to add one DID to a set.
    12→
    13→## Design Principles
    14→
    15→1. **Layer is the unit of authorization** — Each layer has its own permit. No monolith page permits for data access.
    16→2. **Capabilities, not roles** — Permits say what you CAN DO (read, write, sync), not who you ARE.
    17→3. **Layer + permit travel together** — When sending layer data, include the permit. Authorization is inseparable from data.
    18→4. **Consent is bidirectional** — Layer permit authorizes viewer to write to node. Layer consent authorizes node to write to viewer.
    19→5. **LayerUnit is self-contained** — Owns its CRDT doc, permit config, subscribers, version vectors, and broadcast logic.
    20→6. **page_id is transparent** — Apps never see `{page_id}/` prefixes. Added/stripped at the wire boundary only.
    21→
    22→---
    23→
    24→## Part 1: New Permit Model
    25→
    26→### 1.1 Page Access Permit (minimal)
    27→
    28→Authorizes connection to a page's Scribe. No layer data access.
    29→
    30→```json
    31→{
    32→  "type": "page_access",
    33→  "page_id": "abc123",
    34→  "presence": { "visible": true, "can_see_others": true },
    35→  "ephemeral_funcs": ["typing"],
    36→  "dynamic_layer_schemas": {
    37→    "channels/{id}/messages": {
    38→      "type": "map",
    39→      "grant": "open",
    40→      "default_capabilities": { "read": true, "write": true, "sync": true }
    41→    },
    42→    "dms/{id}/messages": {
    43→      "type": "map",
    44→      "grant": "explicit",
    45→      "default_capabilities": { "read": true, "write": true, "sync": true }
    46→    }
    47→  }
    48→}
    49→```
    50→
    51→What moved OUT:
    52→- `layers` block (now per-layer permits)
    53→- `relationship` field (no roles)
    54→- `operations` (replaced by per-layer capabilities)
    55→- `peer_capabilities` (replaced by per-layer capabilities)
    56→- `issue_on` chains (no delegation nesting)
    57→
    58→What stays:
    59→- `presence` config (page-level: are you visible?)
    60→- `ephemeral_funcs` (page-level: what ephemeral events can you send?)
    61→- `dynamic_layer_schemas` (page-level: what patterns can be created?) — but simplified, no role_permissions
    62→
    63→### 1.2 Layer Permit
    64→
    65→Issued per-layer, per-peer. Authorizes the holder to interact with a specific layer on the issuer's system.
    66→
    67→```json
    68→{
    69→  "type": "layer_permit",
    70→  "page_id": "abc123",
    71→  "layer": "channels/general/messages",
    72→  "capabilities": {
    73→    "read": true,
    74→    "write": true,
    75→    "sync": true
    76→  }
    77→}
    78→```
    79→
    80→Direction: **Node → Viewer** (or Owner → Node)

   269→### 3.2 Core methods

   272→impl LayerUnit {
   273→    // --- Creation ---
   274→    pub fn new(doc: Layer, config: LayerConfig) -> Self;
   275→    pub fn new_empty(config: LayerConfig) -> Self;
   276→    pub fn from_snapshot(snapshot: &[u8], config: LayerConfig) -> Result<Self>;
   277→
   278→    // --- Authorization ---
   279→    /// Can we accept a write from this DID?

   281→        self.subscribers.get(did)
   282→            .map(|s| s.permit_capabilities.write)
   283→            .unwrap_or(false)

   285→

   289→            .map(|s| s.consent_token.is_some())
   290→            .unwrap_or(false)
   291→    }
   292→
   293→    /// Can WE write to this layer? (viewer side check)

   295→        self.config.capabilities.write
   296→    }
   297→
   298→    // --- Subscriber management ---

   300→    pub fn remove_subscriber(&mut self, did: &str) -> Option<LayerSubscriber>;
   301→    pub fn set_consent(&mut self, did: &str, consent_token: String);
   302→    pub fn update_subscriber_vector(&mut self, did: &str, vector: Vec<u8>);
   303→
   304→    // --- CRDT operations ---

   306→    pub fn export_snapshot(&self) -> Vec<u8>;
   307→    pub fn export_update_for(&self, did: &str) -> Vec<u8>;
   308→
   309→    // --- Broadcast ---
   310→    /// Broadcast to all subscribers with consent (exclude sender)
   311→    pub fn broadcast_to_subscribers(&self, exclude_did: Option<&str>);
   312→
   313→    // --- Lifecycle ---

   394→### 4.2 Scribe message routing
   395→
   396→```rust
   397→// Before: 50+ lines of permission checks, auth, broadcast in each handler
   398→ScribeMessage::ApplyUpdate { layer_name, update, from_peer, .. } => {
   399→    let unit = self.ensure_warm(&layer_name)?;
   400→    unit.apply_update(&update, from_peer.as_deref())?;
   401→    // LayerUnit handles: permission check, CRDT merge, dirty marking
   402→    // LayerUnit's observer handles: broadcast to subscribers, UI notification
   403→}
   404→
   405→ScribeMessage::Subscribe { did, device_id, broadcast_tx, ephemeral_tx, page_access_permit, layer_permits } => {

   407→    // 2. Store connection info
   408→    state.connections.insert(did.clone(), ConnectionInfo { did, device_id, ephemeral_tx });
   409→
   410→    // 3. For each layer_permit: add subscriber to the LayerUnit
   411→    for (layer_name, permit) in layer_permits {
   412→        let unit = self.ensure_warm(&layer_name)?;
   413→        let capabilities = parse_capabilities(&permit);
   414→        unit.add_subscriber(did.clone(), capabilities, broadcast_tx.clone());
   415→        // Send initial state
   416→        let update = unit.export_update_for(&did);
   417→        broadcast_tx.send(BroadcastPayload { layer_name, update, .. });
   418→    }
   419→}

   422→### 4.3 Lifecycle management
   423→
   424→```rust
   425→impl Scribe {
   426→    /// Load layer from storage if not in memory
   427→    fn ensure_warm(&mut self, layer_name: &str) -> Result<&mut LayerUnit> {
   428→        if self.state.units.contains_key(layer_name) {
   429→            let unit = self.state.units.get_mut(layer_name).unwrap();
   430→            unit.touch();
   431→            return Ok(unit);
   432→        }
   433→
   434→        // Load from storage
   435→        let snapshot = self.state.layer_storage.load_layer(layer_name)?;
   436→        let config = self.state.layer_storage.load_layer_config(layer_name)?;
   437→        let unit = match snapshot {
   438→            Some(data) => LayerUnit::from_snapshot(&data, config)?,
   439→            None => LayerUnit::new_empty(config),
   440→        };
   441→        self.state.units.insert(layer_name.to_string(), unit);
   442→        // Set up Loro observer
   443→        setup_layer_observer(&mut self.state, layer_name);
   444→        Ok(self.state.units.get_mut(layer_name).unwrap())
   445→    }
   446→
   447→    /// Evict cold layers (called periodically, e.g. every 60s)
   448→    fn evict_cold_layers(&mut self) {
   449→        let threshold = Duration::from_secs(300);
   450→        let cold: Vec<String> = self.state.units.iter()
   451→            .filter(|(_, u)| u.is_cold(threshold) && !u.has_subscribers())
   452→            .map(|(name, _)| name.clone())
   453→            .collect();
   454→
   455→        for name in cold {
   456→            if let Some(mut unit) = self.state.units.remove(&name) {
   457→                if let Some(snapshot) = unit.take_dirty_snapshot() {
   458→                    let _ = self.state.layer_storage.save_layer(&name, &snapshot);
   459→                }
   460→            }
   461→        }
   462→    }
   463→}
   464→```

   468→## Part 5: Wire Protocol — Unified Layer Sync
   469→
   470→### 5.1 The single sync pattern
   471→
   472→Every layer sync follows the same pattern:
   473→
   474→```
   475→Sender → Receiver:  LayerSync { layer_name, data, permit }
   476→Receiver → Sender:  LayerConsent { layer_name, consent }
   477→```
   478→
   479→This replaces:
   480→- Initial state delivery (send_initial_state_to_subscriber)
   481→- LayerPermit message
   482→- LayerConsentGrant message
   483→- AuthorizeLayerSubscriber internal message
   484→- DistributeLayerPermits coordinator message
   485→
   486→### 5.2 New wire messages
   487→
   488→```rust
   489→/// Sent when establishing sync for a layer (initial + ongoing discovery)
   490→pub struct LayerSyncMsg {
   491→    pub request_id: String,
   492→    pub page_id: String,
   493→    pub layer_name: String,
   494→    pub data: Vec<u8>,           // snapshot or incremental update
   495→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   496→    pub permit: String,          // layer permit token
   497→}
   498→
   499→/// Response: receiver consents to bidirectional sync
   500→pub struct LayerConsentMsg {
   501→    pub request_id: String,
   502→    pub page_id: String,
   503→    pub layer_name: String,
   504→    pub consent: String,         // consent permit token
   505→}
   506→
   507→/// Ongoing updates (after initial LayerSync + Consent)
   508→pub struct LayerUpdateMsg {
   509→    pub page_id: String,
   510→    pub layer_name: String,
   511→    pub data: Vec<u8>,
   512→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   513→}
   514→```
   515→
   516→### 5.3 Flows
   517→
   518→**Initial connection:**
   519→```
   520→1. Handshake (page_access permit exchange — auth only)
   521→2. Node issues layer permits for all layers the peer should access
   522→3. For each layer:
   523→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   524→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   525→4. Both sides now have: data + authorization
   526→5. Ongoing: LayerUpdate messages (no permit needed)
   527→```
   528→
   529→**New app installed:**
   530→```
   531→1. Node creates app layer, issues layer permits to each peer
   532→2. For each peer:
   533→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data: app_code, permit: { read: true, write: false, sync: true } }
   534→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   535→```
   536→
   537→**Dynamic channel created:**
   538→```
   539→1. Owner creates "channels/did:key:alice/general/messages" locally
   540→2. Owner → Node: LayerUpdate (sync_target rule — no permit needed)
   541→3. Node detects dynamic schema match (grant: "open")
   542→4. Node issues layer permits to all peers with page_access
   543→5. For each peer:
   544→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   545→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   546→```
   547→
   548→**DM (explicit grant):**
   549→```
   550→1. Creator creates "dms/did:key:alice/room1/messages"
   551→2. Creator → Node: LayerUpdate (sync_target)
   552→3. Creator calls add_layer_access(layer, "did:key:bob")
   553→4. Node issues layer permit for Bob only
   554→5. Node → Bob:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   555→   Bob → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   556→```
   557→
   558→### 5.4 Removed wire messages
   559→
   560→- `LayerPermitMsg` → merged into `LayerSyncMsg`
   561→- `LayerConsentGrantMsg` → replaced by `LayerConsentMsg`
   562→- `LayerConsentAckMsg` → no separate ack needed (consent IS the ack)
   563→- `DistributeLayerPermits` coordinator msg → coordinator sends `LayerSync` directly
   564→
   565→### 5.5 Sync target rule
   566→
   567→The viewer always syncs all its layers to its sync_target (the node) without needing a permit. The node is a trusted relay. The viewer's LayerUnit doesn't check `can_push_to(node)` — it pushes unconditionally.
   568→
   569→This is the ONE special case. Everything else goes through permit + consent.

   647→- Token encoding/decoding
   648→
   649→---
   650→
   651→## Part 8: Butler Storage Changes
   652→
   653→### 8.1 Per-layer permit storage
   654→
   655→```rust
   656→// Old: one page permit per (page_id, did)
   657→store_page_permit(page_id, did, token)
   658→
   659→// New: layer permits per (page_id, layer_name, did)
   660→store_layer_permit(page_id, layer_name, did, token)
   661→list_layer_permits(page_id, did) -> Vec<(layer_name, token)>
   662→```
   663→
   664→### 8.2 Consent storage
   665→
   666→```rust
   667→// Per-layer consent per (page_id, layer_name, did)
   668→store_layer_consent(page_id, layer_name, did, consent_token)
   669→get_layer_consent(page_id, layer_name, did) -> Option<token>
   670→```
   671→
   672→### 8.3 What's removed
   673→
   674→- `store_viewer_layer_consent` (old consent model)
   675→- `store_viewer_consent` (old batched consent)
   676→- Role-based permit issuance helpers
   677→
   678→---
   679→
   680→## Part 9: Implementation Phases
   681→
   682→### Phase 1: Rich LayerUnit (scribe only)
   683→
   684→**Goal**: Make LayerUnit self-contained. No external API changes.
   685→
   686→1. Add `subscribers`, `config`, `permit_token`, `last_accessed` to LayerUnit
   687→2. Add methods: `add_subscriber`, `remove_subscriber`, `can_accept_write_from`, `can_push_to`, `broadcast_to_subscribers`, `export_update_for`, `apply_update`
   688→3. Move subscriber VVs from `SubscriberInfo.vectors` into `LayerSubscriber.version_vector`
   689→4. Move broadcast logic from `broadcast.rs` into `LayerUnit::broadcast_to_subscribers()`
   690→5. Move observer authorization check to use `LayerUnit::can_push_to()`
   691→6. Remove `authorized_dids` HashSet
   692→7. Remove `pending_layer_authorizations`
   693→8. Remove `authorize_subscriber_for_layers()`
   694→9. Remove `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber` message handling (becomes no-op or log)
   695→10. Simplify Scribe message handlers to route to LayerUnit methods
   696→
   697→**Tests**: Rewrite unit tests in layer_unit/mod.rs. Integration tests should pass with same intent (layers sync correctly).
   698→
   699→### Phase 2: Per-layer permits + capabilities (gurkha + scribe)
   700→
   701→**Goal**: Replace role-based access with capability-based.
   702→
   703→1. Add `Capabilities` struct to gurkha
   704→2. Add `DynamicGrant::Open` / `DynamicGrant::Explicit` (replace `GrantType::Role`)
   705→3. Add `PermitType::LayerPermit` and `PermitType::LayerConsent`
   706→4. Remove `role_permissions` from `DynamicLayerSchema`
   707→5. Remove `relationship()` usage across codebase
   708→6. Update LayerUnit to parse capabilities from layer permit
   709→7. Update page.lua DSL (remove role definitions, use capability flags)
   710→8. Write new permit_template.json
   711→
   712→**Tests**: Update gurkha unit tests. Update integration tests for new permit format.
   713→
   714→### Phase 3: Unified wire protocol (courier + scribe)
   715→
   716→**Goal**: Layer + permit travel together. Consent replaces complex auth chain.
   717→
   718→1. Add `LayerSyncMsg` and `LayerConsentMsg` wire messages
   719→2. Update PeerActor subscription flow (page_access + layer permits batch)
   720→3. Implement `on_layer_sync` handler (receive data + permit, issue consent)
   721→4. Implement `on_layer_consent` handler (store consent in LayerUnit)
   722→5. Remove `LayerPermitMsg`, `LayerConsentGrantMsg`, `LayerConsentAckMsg`
   723→6. Simplify Coordinator (`DistributeLayerPermits` → direct LayerSync)
   724→7. Remove `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` for open grants (node sends LayerSync directly)
   725→8. Keep `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` only for triggering LayerSync to eligible peers
   726→
   727→**Tests**: Rewrite integration tests (layer_sync.rs). Same intent: static channels sync, dynamic channels sync, viewer writes work, late joiner works.
   728→
   729→### Phase 4: Butler storage + lifecycle (butler + scribe)
   730→
   731→**Goal**: Per-layer permit storage. Cold/warm layer management.
   732→
   733→1. Add per-layer permit storage to Butler
   734→2. Add consent storage to Butler
   735→3. Implement `ensure_warm()` on Scribe
   736→4. Implement `evict_cold_layers()` periodic timer
   737→5. Update layer persistence to co-locate snapshot + permit
   738→6. Remove old page permit storage (or keep for migration)
   739→
   740→**Tests**: Storage unit tests. Lifecycle tests (eviction, reload).
   741→
   742→### Phase 5: page_id transparency + cleanup
   743→
   744→**Goal**: Apps never see page_id. Clean up dead code.
   745→
   746→1. Remove all `normalize_layer_name()` calls inside Scribe (bare names only)
   747→2. Add page_id prefix at PeerActor wire boundary only
   748→3. Strip page_id prefix at PeerActor receive boundary only
   749→4. Update Lua API (scribe:map, scribe:list, scribe:create_layer — no page_id)
   750→5. Remove app-level `page_id .. "/" .. layer_path` concatenation in channels.lua etc.
   751→6. Delete dead code: old consent templates, old authorization functions, etc.
   752→
   753→**Tests**: Update all sample apps. E2E tests.
   754→
   755→---
   756→
   757→## Verification
   758→
   759→After each phase, the following should work:
   760→
   761→```bash
   762→# Build
   763→cargo build -p scribe -p courier -p gurkha -p butler
   764→
   765→# Unit tests
   766→cargo test -p scribe
   767→cargo test -p gurkha
   768→
   769→# Integration tests (rewritten for new API)
   770→cargo test -p integration_tests -- layer_sync --nocapture
   771→
   772→# E2E
   773→python e2e_tests/test_custom_channel.py
   774→```
   775→
   776→Intent of each integration test:
   777→1. Static layer syncs owner → node → viewer
   778→2. Dynamic channel (open grant) syncs to all peers
   779→3. Dynamic channel — viewer can write back
   780→4. Dynamic channel — late joiner receives existing data
   781→5. DM (explicit grant) — only granted DID receives data
   782→6. New app install — peers receive app layer without permit reissue

    19→// Layer Name Normalization
    20→
    21→/// Normalize a layer name by stripping `{page_id}/` prefix if present
    22→///
    23→/// **Context**: Lua apps and wire protocol use prefixed names (`{page_id}/messages`)
    24→/// but Scribe stores layers with bare names (`messages`). This strips the prefix
    25→/// at the Scribe boundary so all internal lookups use consistent bare names.
    26→pub fn normalize_layer_name(name: &str, page_id: &str) -> String {
    27→    let prefix = format!("{}/", page_id);
    28→    if let Some(bare) = name.strip_prefix(&prefix) {
    29→        bare.to_string()
    30→    } else {
    31→        name.to_string()
    32→    }
    33→}
    34→
    35→// Capture Helpers
    36→
    37→/// Shorten a DID to its last 12 characters for compact logging
    38→pub fn short_did(did: &str) -> &str {
    39→    let start = did.len().saturating_sub(12);
    40→    &did[start..]
    41→}
    42→
    43→/// Shorten a layer name by collapsing `did:key:...` segments to `...`
    44→pub fn layer_short(name: &str) -> String {
    45→    name.split('/')
    46→        .map(|seg| {
    47→            if seg.starts_with("did:key:") {
    48→                "..."
    49→            } else {
    50→                seg
    51→            }
    52→        })
    53→        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
    54→        .join("/")
    55→}
    56→
    57→fn decode_permit_summary(token: &str, event_layer_name: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
    58→    let Ok(parsed) = gurkha::Permit::from_token(token) else {
    59→        return serde_json::json!({
    60→            "decode_ok": false,
    61→            "error": "invalid_token",
    62→        });
    63→    };
    64→
    65→    let audience = parsed.audience().unwrap_or_default();
    66→    let issuer = parsed.issuer().unwrap_or_default();
    67→    let token_type = parsed.token_type().unwrap_or_default();
    68→
    69→    let page_id = parsed.page_id().unwrap_or_default();
    70→    let page_prefix = format!("{}/", page_id);
    71→    let layer_cfg = parsed.layers().get(event_layer_name).or_else(|| {
    72→        let bare_layer = event_layer_name
    73→            .strip_prefix(&page_prefix)
    74→            .unwrap_or(event_layer_name);
    75→        parsed.layers().get(bare_layer)
    76→    });
    77→
    78→    let (sync, write) = if let Some(cfg) = layer_cfg {
    79→        (cfg.sync, cfg.write)
    80→    } else {
    81→        (false, false)
    82→    };
    83→
    84→    serde_json::json!({
    85→        "decode_ok": true,
    86→        "audience": audience,
    87→        "issuer": issuer,
    88→        "token_type": token_type,
    89→        "page_id": page_id,
    90→        "layer_name": event_layer_name,
    91→        "permissions": {
    92→            "sync": sync,
    93→            "write": write,
    94→        },
    95→    })
    96→}
    97→
    98→// Sync Configuration
    99→
   100→/// Sync mode derived from permit capabilities
   101→///
   102→/// **Design**: Capability-based, not role-based
   103→/// - Mode is derived from permit's sync configuration
   104→/// - No hardcoded role names in decision logic
   105→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   106→pub enum SyncMode {
   107→    /// Sync to a specific source node (users sync to their node)
   108→    ToSource,
   109→    /// Broadcast to all authorized peers (node mode)
   110→    Broadcast,
   111→}
   112→
   113→impl Default for SyncMode {
   114→    fn default() -> Self {
   115→        SyncMode::Broadcast
   116→    }
   117→}
   118→
   119→/// Sync configuration derived from permit
   120→///
   121→/// **Context**: Determines how this Scribe syncs based on permit capabilities
   122→/// - ToSource: Sync to a specific source node (owner/viewer/customer)
   123→/// - Broadcast: Broadcast to all authorized peers (node)
   124→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   125→pub struct SyncConfig {
   126→    /// Sync mode derived from permit (capability-based)
   127→    pub mode: SyncMode,
   128→    /// For ToSource: node_id to sync to
   129→    /// For Broadcast: None (uses list_authorized_users callback)
   130→    pub sync_target: Option<String>,
   131→}
   132→
   133→// Subscriber Types
   134→
   135→/// Information about a subscribed peer
   136→///
   137→/// **Design**: Stores the parsed permit directly instead of extracted fields.
   138→/// All access checks delegate to gurkha::Permit methods, ensuring consistency.
   139→pub struct SubscriberInfo {
   140→    /// Parsed page permit for all access checks (static layers)
   141→    /// Stores the full permit so we can use its methods directly
   142→    pub permit: gurkha::Permit,
   143→    /// Subscriber's DID (for pattern expansion with {aud})

   145→    pub subscriber_did: String,

   148→    pub is_visible: bool,
   149→    /// Whether this subscriber can see others' presence
   150→    /// Gates whether the presence layer is synced to this peer
   151→    pub can_see_others: bool,
   152→    /// Display name for this subscriber (from permit presence config)
   153→    pub display_name: Option<String>,
   154→    /// Channel to send CRDT broadcasts
   155→    pub broadcast_tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>,
   156→    /// Channel to send ephemeral broadcasts (cursor, typing)
   157→    /// PeerActor creates this, spawns listener that sends datagrams
   158→    pub ephemeral_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<EphemeralOutbound>>,
   159→    /// Their last known state vectors (layer_name → version_vector)
   160→    pub vectors: HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
   161→}

   163→impl SubscriberInfo {
   164→    /// Check if subscriber can receive updates for layer (two-tier)
   165→    ///
   166→    /// **Context**: Used at subscribe time to populate LayerUnit.authorized_dids
   167→    /// **Two-tier**: Checks page permit (static layers) then layer permits (dynamic layers)
   168→    pub fn can_receive_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str) -> bool {
   169→        // Block presence layer for peers who can't see others
   170→        if (layer_name == "presence" || layer_name.ends_with("/presence")) && !self.can_see_others {
   171→            return false;

   174→        if self
   175→            .permit
   176→            .sync_facts()
   177→            .no_incoming_updates
   178→            .contains(&layer_name.to_string())
   179→        {
   180→            return false;
   181→        }
   182→        // Check page permit only (layer permits are now handled via LayerUnit.authorized_dids)
   183→        self.permit
   184→            .can_read_layer(layer_name, page_id, &self.subscriber_did)
   185→    }

   192→    pub fn can_write_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str) -> bool {

   194→            .can_write_layer(layer_name, page_id, &self.subscriber_did)
   195→    }

   318→
   319→impl ScribeState {
   320→    /// Protocol-reserved sync metadata layer name.
   321→    ///
   322→    /// These layers are pairwise and handled by protocol rules, not permit templates.
   323→    fn is_protocol_sync_meta_layer(layer_name: &str) -> bool {
   324→        layer_name.starts_with("__sync_meta/")
   325→    }
   326→
   327→    /// Get the next capture sequence number (monotonically increasing)
   328→    fn next_capture_seq(&self) -> u64 {
   329→        self.capture_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
   330→    }
   331→
   332→    /// Check if a layer should sync based on permit configuration
   333→    ///
   334→    /// **Context**: Used to filter out local-only layers (sync: false) before broadcasting
   335→    /// **Returns**: true if layer should sync, false if local-only
   336→    pub fn should_sync_layer(&self, layer_name: &str) -> bool {
   337→        if Self::is_protocol_sync_meta_layer(layer_name) {
   338→            return true;
   339→        }
   340→
   341→        self.our_permit
   342→            .as_ref()
   343→            .map(|permit| permit.should_sync_layer(layer_name, &self.page_id, &self.our_did))
   344→            .unwrap_or(true) // No permit means sync everything
   345→    }
   346→
   347→    /// Track a newly created sync-enabled layer in our protocol sync metadata map.
   348→    ///
   349→    /// **Context**: Local layer creation (dynamic layer or first-write implicit layer).
   350→    /// **We store**: `__sync_meta/<our_did>[<layer_name>] = {synced: false, version: 1}`.
   351→    /// **Why**: Keep pairwise sync metadata current so node receives layer bootstrap state.
   352→    pub fn track_new_sync_layer_in_meta(&mut self, layer_name: &str) {
   353→        if !self.should_sync_layer(layer_name) || Self::is_protocol_sync_meta_layer(layer_name) {
   354→            return;
   355→        }
   356→
   357→        let sync_meta_layer = format!("__sync_meta/{}", self.our_did);
   358→        let created_sync_meta_layer = if !self.units.contains_key(&sync_meta_layer) {
   359→            let mut unit = LayerUnit::new_empty();
   360→            unit.set_local_only(false);
   361→            self.units.insert(sync_meta_layer.clone(), unit);
   362→            true
   363→        } else {
   364→            false
   365→        };
   366→
   367→        if let Some(unit) = self.units.get_mut(&sync_meta_layer) {
   368→            let map = unit.layer().loro().get_map(sync_meta_layer.as_str());
   369→            if map
   370→                .insert(
   371→                    layer_name,
   372→                    json_to_loro_value(&serde_json::json!({"synced": false, "version": 1})),
   373→                )
   374→                .is_ok()
   375→            {
   376→                unit.layer().commit();
   377→                unit.mark_dirty();
   378→            }
   379→        }
   380→
   381→        if created_sync_meta_layer {
   382→            crate::loro_observer::setup_layer_observer(self, &sync_meta_layer);
   383→        }
   384→    }
   385→
   386→    /// Check if we can write to a layer
   387→    pub fn can_write_layer(&self, layer_name: &str) -> bool {
   388→        self.our_permit
   389→            .as_ref()
   390→            .map(|permit| permit.can_write_layer(layer_name, &self.page_id, &self.our_did))
   391→            .unwrap_or(true) // No permit means full access

### What was added
- **`Capabilities`** struct (`read`, `write`, `sync`) on LayerUnit

### What was removed (clean break, no backward compat)

- **`authorize_subscriber_for_layers()`** — replaced by `add_subscriber_to_layers()`
- 11 call sites of `authorize_did` across actor.rs, apply.rs, dynamic.rs, operations.rs, subscription.rs — all migrated to `add_subscriber`

### What was migrated
- **Observer** (loro_observer.rs): uses `LayerUnit.subscribers()` instead of cross-referencing ScribeState.subscribers + authorized_dids
- **Broadcast** (broadcast.rs): uses `LayerUnit.subscribers()` directly — simpler loop, no two-map cross-reference
- **Reconcile** (reconcile.rs): uses `LayerUnit.subscribers()` for divergence detection
- **Subscription** (subscription.rs): `add_subscriber_to_layers()` adds per-layer subscribers at subscribe time

file.content:
### Phase 2: Per-layer permits + capabilities (gurkha + scribe)

**Goal**: Replace role-based access with capability-based.

1. Add `Capabilities` struct to gurkha
2. Add `DynamicGrant::Open` / `DynamicGrant::Explicit` (replace `GrantType::Role`)
3. Add `PermitType::LayerPermit` and `PermitType::LayerConsent`
4. Remove `role_permissions` from `DynamicLayerSchema`
5. Remove `relationship()` usage across codebase
6. Update LayerUnit to parse capabilities from layer permit
7. Update page.lua DSL (remove role definitions, use capability flags)
8. Write new permit_template.json

**Tests**: Update gurkha unit tests. Update integration tests for new permit format.

### Phase 3: Unified wire protocol (courier + scribe)

**Goal**: Layer + permit travel together. Consent replaces complex auth chain.

1. Add `LayerSyncMsg` and `LayerConsentMsg` wire messages
2. Update PeerActor subscription flow (page_access + layer permits batch)
3. Implement `on_layer_sync` handler (receive data + permit, issue consent)
4. Implement `on_layer_consent` handler (store consent in LayerUnit)
5. Remove `LayerPermitMsg`, `LayerConsentGrantMsg`, `LayerConsentAckMsg`
6. Simplify Coordinator (`DistributeLayerPermits` → direct LayerSync)
7. Remove `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` for open grants (node sends LayerSync directly)
8. Keep `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` only for triggering LayerSync to eligible peers

**Tests**: Rewrite integration tests (layer_sync.rs). Same intent: static channels sync, dynamic channels sync, viewer writes work, late joiner works.

### Phase 4: Butler storage + lifecycle (butler + scribe)

**Goal**: Per-layer permit storage. Cold/warm layer management.

1. Add per-layer permit storage to Butler
2. Add consent storage to Butler
3. Implement `ensure_warm()` on Scribe
4. Implement `evict_cold_layers()` periodic timer
5. Update layer persistence to co-locate snapshot + permit
6. Remove old page permit storage (or keep for migration)

**Tests**: Storage unit tests. Lifecycle tests (eviction, reload).

### Phase 5: page_id transparency + cleanup

**Goal**: Apps never see page_id. Clean up dead code.

1. Remove all `normalize_layer_name()` calls inside Scribe (bare names only)
2. Add page_id prefix at PeerActor wire boundary only
3. Strip page_id prefix at PeerActor receive boundary only
4. Update Lua API (scribe:map, scribe:list, scribe:create_layer — no page_id)
5. Remove app-level `page_id .. "/" .. layer_path` concatenation in channels.lua etc.
6. Delete dead code: old consent templates, old authorization functions, etc.

**Tests**: Update all sample apps. E2E tests.

---

## Verification

1→//! Gurkha - Pure Permit Authorization Domain
     2→//!
     3→//! Standalone permit business logic with zero infrastructure dependencies.
     4→//! Permits are extended UCAN tokens with facts-based authorization.
     5→//!
     6→//! ## Design Principles
     7→//!
     8→//! - **Pure domain logic** - No database, no crypto utilities, no services
     9→//! - **Stateless functions** - Receives key bytes, returns results
    10→//! - **OCaml-ready** - Can be replaced with OCaml implementation
    11→//! - **Facts-driven** - All authorization in facts field, no typed wrappers
    12→//!
    13→//! ## Module Structure (V3: Facts-Only)
    14→//!
    15→//! - `types` - Domain types (Capability, DocType, SyncDecision, SyncFacts)
    16→//! - `parser` - Permit, DelegationTemplate, PermitCore (facts-based parsing)
    17→//! - `decision` - Decision/inference logic (pure facts-based logic)
    18→//! - `crypto` - UCAN token signing (Ed25519 + CID)
    19→//! - `service` - Stateless permit functions (takes key bytes, returns permits)
    20→//! - `errors` - GurkhaError types

    88→/// Parse and validate `authorized_peers` fact value.
    89→///
    90→/// Semantics:
    91→/// - missing or null => role-based distribution (`None`)
    92→/// - array of DIDs   => explicit recipients (`Some(Vec<String>)`)
    93→pub fn parse_authorized_peers_fact(
    94→    value: Option<&serde_json::Value>,
    95→) -> PermitResult<Option<Vec<String>>> {
    96→    let Some(value) = value else {
    97→        return Ok(None);
    98→    };
    99→
   100→    if value.is_null() {
   101→        return Ok(None);
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    let arr = value.as_array().ok_or_else(|| {
   105→        PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   106→            "authorized_peers must be null or an array of DIDs".to_string(),
   107→        )
   108→    })?;
   109→
   110→    if arr.is_empty() {
   111→        return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   112→            "authorized_peers must be null for role-based distribution or a non-empty DID list"
   113→                .to_string(),
   114→        ));
   115→    }
   116→
   117→    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
   118→    let mut peers = Vec::new();
   119→    for entry in arr {
   120→        let did = entry
   121→            .as_str()
   122→            .ok_or_else(|| {
   123→                PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   124→                    "authorized_peers entries must be strings".to_string(),
   125→                )
   126→            })?
   127→            .trim();
   128→
   129→        if did.is_empty() {
   130→            return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   131→                "authorized_peers entries must be non-empty DIDs".to_string(),
   132→            ));
   133→        }
   134→
   135→        if !did.starts_with("did:") {
   136→            return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(format!(
   137→                "authorized_peers entry '{}' is not a DID",
   138→                did
   139→            )));
   140→        }
   141→
   142→        if seen.insert(did.to_string()) {
   143→            peers.push(did.to_string());
   144→        }
   145→    }
   146→
   147→    if peers.is_empty() {
   148→        return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   149→            "authorized_peers must contain at least one DID".to_string(),
   150→        ));
   151→    }
   152→
   153→    Ok(Some(peers))
   154→}

   317→    /// This creates the facts structure that will be embedded in the delegated token.
   318→    /// Role-agnostic: only includes capabilities and patterns, no role-based logic.
   319→    pub fn to_facts(&self) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {
   320→        let mut facts = serde_json::Map::new();
   321→
   322→        // Add token_type
   323→        facts.insert(
   324→            "token_type".to_string(),
   325→            serde_json::Value::String(self.token_type.clone()),
   326→        );
   327→
   328→        // Add peer_capabilities
   329→        facts.insert(
   330→            "peer_capabilities".to_string(),
   331→            self.peer_capabilities.to_json(),
   332→        );
   333→
   334→        // Add operations (required for delegation chain - e.g., add_pages permission)
   335→        if !self.operations.is_empty() {
   336→            let ops_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   337→                .operations
   338→                .iter()
   339→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), serde_json::Value::String(v.clone())))
   340→                .collect();
   341→            facts.insert(
   342→                "operations".to_string(),
   343→                serde_json::Value::Object(ops_json),
   344→            );
   345→        }
   346→
   347→        // Add auth_capabilities
   348→        if !self.auth_capabilities.is_empty() {
   349→            let auth_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   350→                .auth_capabilities
   351→                .iter()
   352→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   353→                .collect();
   354→            facts.insert(
   355→                "auth_capabilities".to_string(),
   356→                serde_json::Value::Object(auth_json),
   357→            );
   358→        }
   359→
   360→        // Add layer_patterns
   361→        if !self.layer_patterns.is_empty() {
   362→            let patterns_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   363→                .layer_patterns
   364→                .iter()
   365→                .map(|(pattern, config)| {
   366→                    (
   367→                        pattern.clone(),
   368→                        serde_json::json!({
   369→                            "create": config.create,
   370→                            "sync": config.sync,
   371→                            "write": config.write
   372→                        }),
   373→                    )
   374→                })
   375→                .collect();
   376→            facts.insert(

   385→                .layers
   386→                .iter()

   390→                    layer_obj.insert("write".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.write));
   391→                    if let Some(ref t) = config.layer_type {

   393→                    }
   394→                    (name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(layer_obj))

   398→        }

     2→page("Group Chat", "1.0.0")
     3→
     4→-- =============================================================================
     5→-- Roles
     6→-- =============================================================================
     7→
     8→role("owner", {
     9→    can_share = true,
    10→    can_delegate = true
    11→})
    12→
    13→role("collaborator", {
    14→    parent = "owner"
    15→})
    16→
    17→role("node", {
    18→    parent = "owner",
    19→    can_relay = true
    20→})
    21→
    22→-- =============================================================================
    23→-- Layers
    24→-- =============================================================================
    25→
    26→-- Dynamic per-channel messages — LoroMap keyed by message ID
    27→layer("channels/{channel_id}/messages", "map", {
    28→    owner = {"read", "write", "sync"},
    29→    collaborator = {"read", "write", "sync"},
    30→    node = {"read", "write", "sync", "create"},
    31→
    32→    validate = function(ops, ctx)
    33→        for _, op in ipairs(ops) do
    34→            if op.op == "update" and op.old_value then
    35→                local old = op.old_value
    36→                local new = op.value
    37→                if (new.text ~= old.text or new.deleted ~= old.deleted or new.edited ~= old.edited)
    38→                   and ctx.from_did ~= old.sender_did then
    39→                    return false, "Only sender can edit their own message"
    40→                end
    41→            end
    42→        end
    43→        return true, nil
    44→    end
    45→})
    46→

1190→/// Match a layer path against a dynamic layer schema pattern (issuance-side only)
  1191→///
  1192→/// Used at dynamic layer creation time to validate that the node has authority
  1193→/// to create a layer of this type.
  1194→///
  1195→/// **Pattern:** `{id}` matches any single path segment
  1196→///
  1197→/// **Examples:**
  1198→/// - `channels/announcements/messages` matches `channels/{id}/messages`
  1199→/// - `dms/uuid-123/messages` matches `dms/{id}/messages`
  1200→/// - `orders/uuid-456` matches `orders/{id}`
  1201→pub fn matches_schema_pattern(layer_path: &str, schema_pattern: &str) -> bool {
  1202→    let path_parts: Vec<&str> = layer_path.split('/').collect();
  1203→    let pattern_parts: Vec<&str> = schema_pattern.split('/').collect();
  1204→
  1205→    if path_parts.len() != pattern_parts.len() {
  1206→        return false;
  1207→    }
  1208→
  1209→    path_parts
  1210→        .iter()
  1211→        .zip(pattern_parts.iter())
  1212→        .all(|(path_seg, pat_seg)| *pat_seg == "{id}" || path_seg == pat_seg)
  1213→}
  1214→
  1215→/// Check access across a page permit + set of layer permits (two-tier model)
  1216→///
  1217→/// Convenience function that delegates to `decision::can_access_with_layer_permits`.
  1218→/// Checks if any permit in the set grants the requested access.
  1219→///
  1220→/// Access check = page permit layers ∪ all layer permit layers ∪ schema fallback
  1221→pub fn can_access_with_layer_permits(
  1222→    page_permit: &Permit,
  1223→    layer_permits: &[Permit],
  1224→    layer_name: &str,
  1225→    page_id: &str,
  1226→    did: &str,
  1227→) -> bool {
  1228→    crate::decision::can_access_with_layer_permits(
  1229→        page_permit,
  1230→        layer_permits,
  1231→        layer_name,
  1232→        page_id,
  1233→        did,
  1234→        "read",
  1235→    )
  1236→}
  1237→
  1238→/// Match layer name against pattern with path-segment wildcards
  1239→///
  1240→/// **Pattern:** `*` matches any single path segment (delimited by `/`)
  1241→///
  1242→/// **Examples:**
  1243→/// - `shop123/*/did:key:abc` matches `shop123/orders/did:key:abc`
  1244→/// - `shop123/*/*` matches `shop123/orders/did:key:abc`
  1245→/// - `shop123/*` does NOT match `shop123/orders/did:key:abc` (different segment count)
  1246→pub fn matches_wildcard(layer_name: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
  1247→    let layer_parts: Vec<&str> = layer_name.split('/').collect();
  1248→    let pattern_parts: Vec<&str> = pattern.split('/').collect();
  1249→
  1250→    if layer_parts.len() != pattern_parts.len() {
  1251→        return false;
  1252→    }
  1253→
  1254→    layer_parts
  1255→        .iter()
  1256→        .zip(pattern_parts.iter())
  1257→        .all(|(layer, pat)| *pat == "*" || layer == pat)
  1258→}

1→//! Permit Service - Stateless permit token operations
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides stateless functions for permit token generation and delegation.
     4→//! All functions take signing key bytes and return signed permits.
     5→//!
     6→//! Usage:
     7→//! ```ignore
     8→//! let secret_key: [u8; 32] = identity.secret_signing_key();
     9→//! let (token, cid) = gurkha::issue_one_time(&secret_key, "owner").await?;
    10→//! ```
    11→
    12→use crate::crypto;
    13→use crate::decision;
    14→use crate::errors::{ServiceError, ServiceResult};
    15→use crate::parser::Permit;
    16→use base64::{engine::general_purpose, Engine as _};
    17→use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
    18→use tracing::{info, instrument, trace};
    19→
    20→/// Issue a one-time connection token
    21→///
    22→/// Used for initial device pairing (QR codes, connection strings).
    23→/// Facts-only approach - relationship determines permissions.
    24→///
    25→/// # Arguments
    26→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
    27→/// * `relationship` - "owner", "node", "peer_user", or "peer_node"
    28→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes), fields(relationship = %relationship, token_type = "one_time"))]
    29→pub async fn issue_one_time(
    30→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
    31→    relationship: &str,
    32→) -> ServiceResult<(String, String)> {
    33→    trace!("Issuing one-time connection token");
    34→
    35→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
    36→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    37→
    38→    let decision = decision::decide_one_time_token(&verifying_key, relationship)?;
    39→    trace!("Token decision created");
    40→
    41→    let (token, cid) = crypto::sign_permit(signing_key_bytes, &decision).await?;
    42→
    43→    info!("One-time token generated: cid={}", cid);
    44→    Ok((token, cid))
    45→}
    46→
    47→/// Issue a peer connection token
    48→///
    49→/// Establishes bidirectional peer connection with signed permit.
    50→/// Facts-only approach - no domain needed, relationship determines permissions.
    51→///
    52→/// # Arguments
    53→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
    54→/// * `peer_pubkey` - Base64-encoded public key of the peer
    55→/// * `relationship` - "owner", "node", "peer_user", or "peer_node"
    56→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes, peer_pubkey), fields(relationship = %relationship, token_type = "peer_connection"))]
    57→pub async fn issue_peer_connection(
    58→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
    59→    peer_pubkey: &str,
    60→    relationship: &str,
    61→) -> ServiceResult<String> {
    62→    trace!("Issuing peer connection token");
    63→
    64→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
    65→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    66→
    67→    let decision = decision::decide_peer_connection(&verifying_key, peer_pubkey, relationship)?;
    68→
    69→    let (token, _cid) = crypto::sign_permit(signing_key_bytes, &decision).await?;
    70→
    71→    info!("Peer connection token generated");
    72→    Ok(token)

595→/// Issue a layer permit granting access to a single dynamic layer
   596→///
   597→/// **Context**: Node detected a new dynamic layer and issues permits to eligible peers.
   598→/// Contains just one layer in facts, proof chain references node's page permit.
   599→///
   600→/// # Arguments
   601→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - Node's 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
   602→/// * `node_permit` - Node's page permit token (used as proof)
   603→/// * `audience` - Recipient DID
   604→/// * `page_id` - Page identifier
   605→/// * `layer_name` - Fully resolved layer path (e.g., "page1/channels/did:key:alice/general/messages")
   606→/// * `config` - Layer permissions (sync, write)
   607→///
   608→/// # Returns
   609→/// * `Ok((token, cid))` - The layer permit token and its CID
   610→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes, node_permit, config), fields(page_id = %page_id, layer_name = %layer_name, token_type = "layer_permit"))]
   611→pub async fn issue_layer_permit(
   612→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
   613→    node_permit: &str,
   614→    audience: &str,
   615→    page_id: &str,
   616→    layer_name: &str,
   617→    config: crate::parser::LayerConfig,
   618→    intent_cid: Option<&str>,
   619→) -> ServiceResult<(String, String)> {
   620→    trace!("Issuing layer permit for dynamic layer");
   621→
   622→    // Build facts with exactly one layer
   623→    let mut facts = serde_json::Map::new();
   624→    facts.insert("token_type".to_string(), serde_json::json!("layer_permit"));
   625→    facts.insert("page_id".to_string(), serde_json::json!(page_id));
   626→    facts.insert("relationship".to_string(), serde_json::json!("layer_permit"));
   627→
   628→    // Single layer entry
   629→    let mut layer_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
   630→    layer_obj.insert("sync".to_string(), serde_json::json!(config.sync));

    54→}

    56→impl UpdateContext {

    60→    /// **Note**: Permission checks are done separately (may reject before context is useful)

   319→    pub fn to_facts(&self) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {

   321→

   333→
   334→        // Add operations (required for delegation chain - e.g., add_pages permission)

   339→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), serde_json::Value::String(v.clone())))
   340→                .collect();
   341→            facts.insert(
