   344→            );
   345→        }
   346→
   347→        // Add auth_capabilities
   348→        if !self.auth_capabilities.is_empty() {
   349→            let auth_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   350→                .auth_capabilities
   351→                .iter()
   352→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   353→                .collect();
   354→            facts.insert(
   355→                "auth_capabilities".to_string(),
   356→                serde_json::Value::Object(auth_json),
   357→            );
   358→        }
   359→
   360→        // Add layer_patterns
   361→        if !self.layer_patterns.is_empty() {
   362→            let patterns_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   363→                .layer_patterns
   364→                .iter()
   365→                .map(|(pattern, config)| {
   366→                    (
   367→                        pattern.clone(),
   368→                        serde_json::json!({
   369→                            "create": config.create,
   370→                            "sync": config.sync,
   371→                            "write": config.write
   372→                        }),
   373→                    )
   374→                })
   375→                .collect();
   376→            facts.insert(
   377→                "layer_patterns".to_string(),
   378→                serde_json::Value::Object(patterns_json),
   379→            );
   380→        }
   381→
   382→        // Add fixed layers
   383→        if !self.layers.is_empty() {
   384→            let layers_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   385→                .layers
   386→                .iter()
   387→                .map(|(name, config)| {
   388→                    let mut layer_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
   389→                    layer_obj.insert("sync".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.sync));
   390→                    layer_obj.insert("write".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.write));
   391→                    if let Some(ref t) = config.layer_type {
   392→                        layer_obj.insert("type".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(t.clone()));
   393→                    }
   394→                    (name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(layer_obj))
   395→                })
   396→                .collect();
   397→            facts.insert("layers".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(layers_json));
   398→        }
   399→
   400→        // Add relationship (for logging only)
   401→        if let Some(rel) = &self.relationship {
   402→            facts.insert(
   403→                "relationship".to_string(),
   404→                serde_json::Value::String(rel.clone()),
   405→            );
   406→        }
   407→
   408→        // Add issue_on (self-describing templates for what to issue on actions)
   409→        if !self.issue_on.is_empty() {
   410→            let issue_on_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   411→                .issue_on
   412→                .iter()
   413→                .map(|(action, template)| {
   414→                    (
   415→                        action.clone(),
   416→                        serde_json::Value::Object(template.to_facts()),
   417→                    )
   418→                })
   419→                .collect();
   420→            facts.insert(
   421→                "issue_on".to_string(),
   422→                serde_json::Value::Object(issue_on_json),
   423→            );
   424→        }
   425→
   426→        // Add presence configuration
   427→        if let Some(ref presence) = self.presence {
   428→            let mut presence_json = serde_json::Map::new();
   429→            presence_json.insert(
   430→                "visible".to_string(),
   431→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.visible),
   432→            );
   433→            presence_json.insert(
   434→                "can_see_others".to_string(),
   435→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.can_see_others),
   436→            );
   437→            if let Some(ref name) = presence.name {
   438→                presence_json.insert("name".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(name.clone()));
   439→            }
   440→            facts.insert(
   441→                "presence".to_string(),
   442→                serde_json::Value::Object(presence_json),
   443→            );
   444→        }
   445→
   446→        // Add ephemeral_funcs (allowed ephemeral function names)
   447→        if !self.ephemeral_funcs.is_empty() {
   448→            let funcs: Vec<serde_json::Value> = self
   449→                .ephemeral_funcs
   450→                .iter()
   451→                .map(|f| serde_json::Value::String(f.clone()))
   452→                .collect();
   453→            facts.insert(
   454→                "ephemeral_funcs".to_string(),
   455→                serde_json::Value::Array(funcs),
   456→            );
   457→        }
   458→
   459→        // Add dynamic_layer_schemas
   460→        if !self.dynamic_layer_schemas.is_empty() {
   461→            let schemas_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   462→                .dynamic_layer_schemas

   486→                    "authorized_peers".to_string(),

1→//! Lua Runtime - Unified Lua runtime for Osvauld
     2→//!
     3→//! Single runtime implementation used by both shell (viewer) and kunki (node).
     4→//!
     5→//! ## Features
     6→//!
     7→//! - **Unified Runtime**: One `LuaRuntime` for all contexts
     8→//! - **Timer Support**: JS-style `setTimeout`/`setInterval` via Scheduler
     9→//! - **Validation**: Built-in `validate_ops()` method for permission checking
    10→//! - **Async Event Loop**: Uses `tokio::select!` for efficient multiplexing
    11→//! - **Optional UI**: Enable/disable UI bindings based on configuration
    12→//!
    13→//! ## Architecture
    14→//!
    15→//! ```text
    16→//! ┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
    17→//! │     sthalam     │     │     kunki       │
    18→//! │  (ui_enabled)   │     │ (ui_disabled)   │
    19→//! └────────┬────────┘     └────────┬────────┘
    20→//!          │                       │
    21→//!          │  LuaRuntimeConfig     │

    23→//!                      │

1→--[[
     2→Osvauld App API Module
     3→
     4→Provides utilities for apps to expose functions for external calling (via control server).
     5→
     6→Usage in apps:
     7→    -- Register a function for external calling
     8→    api.export("add_product", add_product)
     9→
    10→    -- Add description for AI assistance (optional)
    11→    api.describe("add_product", {
    12→        description = "Add a new product to the catalog",
    13→        params = {
    14→            {name = "name", type = "string", description = "Product name"},
    15→            {name = "price", type = "number", description = "Price in dollars"},
    16→        },
    17→        returns = "product_id",
    18→        effects = {"products layer updated", "UI refreshes product list"},
    19→        syncs = {"products layer propagates to all peers"},
    20→    })
    21→
    22→The @ai annotations in LDoc comments are also supported:
    23→    --- @ai Adds product to catalog.
    24→    --- @ai Effects: products layer updated, product_count incremented
    25→    --- @ai Syncs: products layer to all peers
    26→    function add_product(name, price)
    27→        -- ...
    28→    end
    29→--]]
    30→
    31→local api = {}
    32→
    33→-- Registry of exported functions
    34→-- Maps function_name -> function
    35→api._exports = {}
    36→
    37→-- Registry of function descriptions (for AI assistance)
    38→-- Maps function_name -> description table
    39→api._descriptions = {}
    40→
    41→--- Export a function for external calling
    42→--- @param name string The name to expose the function as
    43→--- @param fn function The function to export
    44→--- @param description table|nil Optional description table
    45→function api.export(name, fn, description)
    46→    if type(name) ~= "string" then
    47→        error("api.export: name must be a string, got " .. type(name))
    48→    end
    49→    if type(fn) ~= "function" then
    50→        error("api.export: fn must be a function, got " .. type(fn))
    51→    end
    52→
    53→    api._exports[name] = fn
    54→
    55→    -- Also set as global for backward compatibility with direct calls
    56→    _G[name] = fn
    57→
    58→    if description then
    59→        api._descriptions[name] = description
    60→    end
    61→end
    62→
    63→--- Add or update description for an exported function
    64→--- @param name string Function name
    65→--- @param description table Description table with fields:
    66→---   - description: string - What the function does
    67→---   - params: table[] - Parameter descriptions [{name, type, description}, ...]
    68→---   - returns: string - What the function returns
    69→---   - effects: string[] - Side effects (UI changes, layer updates)
    70→---   - syncs: string[] - What syncs to other peers
    71→function api.describe(name, description)
    72→    if type(name) ~= "string" then
    73→        error("api.describe: name must be a string")
    74→    end
    75→    if type(description) ~= "table" then
    76→        error("api.describe: description must be a table")
    77→    end
    78→
    79→    api._descriptions[name] = description
    80→end
    81→
    82→--- Call an exported function by name
    83→--- Used by the control server to invoke functions
    84→--- @param name string Function name
    85→--- @param ... any Arguments to pass
    86→--- @return any Result from the function
    87→function api.call(name, ...)
    88→    local fn = api._exports[name]
    89→    if not fn then
    90→        error("api.call: function '" .. name .. "' not exported")
    91→    end
    92→    return fn(...)
    93→end
    94→
    95→--- List all exported function names
    96→--- @return string[] List of exported function names
    97→function api.list()
    98→    local names = {}
    99→    for name, _ in pairs(api._exports) do
   100→        table.insert(names, name)
   101→    end
   102→    table.sort(names)
   103→    return names
   104→end
   105→
   106→--- Get description for a function
   107→--- @param name string Function name
   108→--- @return table|nil Description table or nil if not described
   109→function api.get_description(name)
   110→    return api._descriptions[name]
   111→end
   112→
   113→--- Get all descriptions
   114→--- @return table Map of function_name -> description
   115→function api.get_all_descriptions()
   116→    return api._descriptions
   117→end
   118→
   119→--- Check if a function is exported
   120→--- @param name string Function name
   121→--- @return boolean
   122→function api.has(name)
   123→    return api._exports[name] ~= nil
   124→end
   125→
   126→return api
   127→

### 2. PAGE.LUA SYNTAX & STRUCTURE

The page.lua files define three main entities:

#### **A. `role()` Function**

```lua
role("owner", {
    can_share = true,      -- Can delegate permits to others
    can_delegate = true,   -- Can perform delegation actions
    parent = nil,          -- Optional: inherit from parent role
})

role("collaborator", {
    parent = "owner"       -- Inherits permissions from owner
})

role("node", {
    parent = "owner",
    can_relay = true       -- Can relay data to other peers
})
```

**Key Points:**
- Roles define permission groups (labels for capability bundles)
- `parent` creates inheritance hierarchy
- Special flags: `can_share`, `can_delegate`, `can_relay`

#### **B. `layer()` Function**

```lua
-- Static layer
layer("navigation", "map", {
    owner = {"read", "write"},
    collaborator = {"read", "write"},
    node = {"read", "write"}
})

-- Dynamic layer (pattern with {aud} placeholder)
layer("orders/{aud}", "list", {
    owner = {"read", "sync"},
    ["{aud}"] = {"read", "write", "sync"},  -- Each user sees own orders
    node = {"read", "sync", "create"},
    
    -- Optional: Validation function
    validate = function(ops, ctx)
        for _, op in ipairs(ops) do
            if op.op == "insert" and op.value then
                local status = op.value.status or "pending"
                if status ~= "pending" then
                    return false, "New orders must start in pending state"
                end
            end
        end
        return true, nil
    end
})

-- Derived layer (read from source, transform via node)
layer("derived/orders_summary", "map", {
    owner = {"read", "sync"},
    node = {"write"},
    
    derive_from = "orders/*",  -- Source pattern
    transform = function(source, item)
        return {
            id = item.id,
            status = item.status,
            total = item.total,
            customer_did = source
        }
    end
})
```

**Layer Permissions:**
- `read` - Can read/sync layer content
- `write` - Can create/modify items (client-side)
- `sync` - Can receive sync updates
- `create` - Can create NEW layers matching pattern (node-side)

**Special Layer Patterns:**
- `{aud}` - Expands to viewer DID (for per-user layers like `orders/did:key:alice`)
- `{page_id}` - Page ID prefix (already handled by framework)
- `channels/{channel_id}/messages` - Multi-level dynamic patterns

#### **C. `app()` Function**

```lua
app("Group Chat", {
    client = {
        ui = "group-chat/app.slint",
        logic = "group-chat/app.lua",
        tick = true  -- Optional: enable timer tick
    },
    node = {
        logic = "shop-owner/node.lua",  -- Optional: node-side logic
        tick = true
    },
    for_role = {"owner", "collaborator"}  -- Which roles can access
})
```

**Sections:**
- `client` - UI (Slint) and logic (Lua) for client apps
- `node` - Optional node-side derivation/processing logic
- `for_role` - Role restrictions (can be string or array)

            }

### 7. HOW RELATIONSHIP() IS USED FOR AUTHORIZATION

**Important**: `relationship()` itself is NOT used for authorization decisions. Instead:

1. **Template Selection** (gurkha/decision):
   - `relationship` parameter tells gurkha which template block to use
   - Templates are looked up: owner→node→viewer hierarchies
   - Example: relationship="node" loads `permit_template.owner_template.issue_on.node`

2. **Capability Extraction** (from template):
   - Actual auth is based on: `peer_capabilities`, `operations`, `layers`

### 2. PAGE.LUA SYNTAX & STRUCTURE

The page.lua files define three main entities:

#### **A. `role()` Function**

```lua
role("owner", {
    can_share = true,      -- Can delegate permits to others
    can_delegate = true,   -- Can perform delegation actions
    parent = nil,          -- Optional: inherit from parent role
})

role("collaborator", {
    parent = "owner"       -- Inherits permissions from owner
})

role("node", {
    parent = "owner",
    can_relay = true       -- Can relay data to other peers
})
```

**Key Points:**
- Roles define permission groups (labels for capability bundles)
- `parent` creates inheritance hierarchy
- Special flags: `can_share`, `can_delegate`, `can_relay`

#### **B. `layer()` Function**

```lua
-- Static layer
layer("navigation", "map", {
    owner = {"read", "write"},
    collaborator = {"read", "write"},
    node = {"read", "write"}
})

-- Dynamic layer (pattern with {aud} placeholder)
layer("orders/{aud}", "list", {
    owner = {"read", "sync"},
    ["{aud}"] = {"read", "write", "sync"},  -- Each user sees own orders
    node = {"read", "sync", "create"},
    
    -- Optional: Validation function
    validate = function(ops, ctx)
        for _, op in ipairs(ops) do
            if op.op == "insert" and op.value then
                local status = op.value.status or "pending"
                if status ~= "pending" then
                    return false, "New orders must start in pending state"
                end
            end
        end
        return true, nil
    end
})

-- Derived layer (read from source, transform via node)
layer("derived/orders_summary", "map", {
    owner = {"read", "sync"},
    node = {"write"},
    
    derive_from = "orders/*",  -- Source pattern
    transform = function(source, item)
        return {
            id = item.id,
            status = item.status,
            total = item.total,
            customer_did = source
        }
    end
})
```

**Layer Permissions:**
- `read` - Can read/sync layer content
- `write` - Can create/modify items (client-side)
- `sync` - Can receive sync updates
- `create` - Can create NEW layers matching pattern (node-side)

**Special Layer Patterns:**
- `{aud}` - Expands to viewer DID (for per-user layers like `orders/did:key:alice`)
- `{page_id}` - Page ID prefix (already handled by framework)
- `channels/{channel_id}/messages` - Multi-level dynamic patterns

```lua
app("Group Chat", {
    client = {
        ui = "group-chat/app.slint",
        logic = "group-chat/app.lua",
        tick = true  -- Optional: enable timer tick
    },
    node = {

    },
    for_role = {"owner", "collaborator"}  -- Which roles can access
})
```

**Sections:**
- `client` - UI (Slint) and logic (Lua) for client apps
- `node` - Optional node-side derivation/processing logic
- `for_role` - Role restrictions (can be string or array)

1→# Plan: Layer-Centric Architecture
     2→
     3→## Problem Statement
     4→
     5→The current authorization system has three fundamental issues:
     6→
     7→1. **Monolith page permits** — A single page permit lists every layer, every role's permissions, nested `issue_on` delegation chains, and `dynamic_layer_schemas`. The permit_template.json is 957 lines with 6+ copies of the same layer block. Installing a new app requires reissuing every peer's page permit.
     8→
     9→2. **Role-based access** — Authorization is tied to role names ("owner", "collaborator", "viewer", "node"). Code checks `allowed_roles.contains(role)` and `role_permissions.get(role)`. This prevents fine-grained capability control.
    10→
    11→3. **Eager authorization cache** — `authorized_dids: HashSet<String>` on each LayerUnit is populated from 11+ disconnected call sites, causing race conditions, bugs (viewer writes to dynamic channels fail), and a complex wire protocol chain just to add one DID to a set.
    12→
    13→## Design Principles
    14→
    15→1. **Layer is the unit of authorization** — Each layer has its own permit. No monolith page permits for data access.
    16→2. **Capabilities, not roles** — Permits say what you CAN DO (read, write, sync), not who you ARE.
    17→3. **Layer + permit travel together** — When sending layer data, include the permit. Authorization is inseparable from data.
    18→4. **Consent is bidirectional** — Layer permit authorizes viewer to write to node. Layer consent authorizes node to write to viewer.
    19→5. **LayerUnit is self-contained** — Owns its CRDT doc, permit config, subscribers, version vectors, and broadcast logic.
    20→6. **page_id is transparent** — Apps never see `{page_id}/` prefixes. Added/stripped at the wire boundary only.
    21→

    23→
    24→## Part 1: New Permit Model
    25→
    26→### 1.1 Page Access Permit (minimal)
    27→
    28→Authorizes connection to a page's Scribe. No layer data access.
    29→
    30→```json
    31→{
    32→  "type": "page_access",
    33→  "page_id": "abc123",
    34→  "presence": { "visible": true, "can_see_others": true },
    35→  "ephemeral_funcs": ["typing"],
    36→  "dynamic_layer_schemas": {

    39→      "grant": "open",
    40→      "default_capabilities": { "read": true, "write": true, "sync": true }
    41→    },
    42→    "dms/{id}/messages": {

    44→      "grant": "explicit",
    45→      "default_capabilities": { "read": true, "write": true, "sync": true }
    46→    }
    47→  }
    48→}
    49→```
    50→
    51→What moved OUT:

    55→- `peer_capabilities` (replaced by per-layer capabilities)

    63→### 1.2 Layer Permit

   228→    loro_sub: Option<loro::Subscription>, // observer handle
   229→
   230→    // === Authorization (from permit) ===
   231→    config: LayerConfig,                 // cached capabilities: read, write, sync
   232→    permit_token: Option<String>,        // raw permit token (viewer side)
   233→    is_dynamic: bool,                    // created via dynamic schema
   234→
   235→    // === Subscriber state (populated on node side) ===
   236→    subscribers: HashMap<String, LayerSubscriber>,  // did → subscriber
   237→
   238→    // === Lifecycle ===
   239→    last_accessed: std::time::Instant,   // for cold/warm eviction
   240→}
   241→
   242→/// Per-subscriber state within a LayerUnit (node side)
   243→pub struct LayerSubscriber {
   244→    /// What this subscriber can do (issued by us)
   245→    pub permit_capabilities: Capabilities,
   246→    /// Their consent (authorizes us to push to them)
   247→    pub consent_token: Option<String>,
   248→    /// Their last known version vector for incremental sync
   249→    pub version_vector: Vec<u8>,
   250→    /// Channel to send broadcasts
   251→    pub broadcast_tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>,
   252→}
   253→
   254→/// Cached capabilities from a permit
   255→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   256→pub struct Capabilities {
   257→    pub read: bool,
   258→    pub write: bool,
   259→    pub sync: bool,
   260→}
   261→
   262→/// Cached page-level config from page_access permit
   263→pub struct LayerConfig {
   264→    pub capabilities: Capabilities,     // our capabilities for this layer
   265→    pub is_local_only: bool,            // sync: false
   266→}
   267→```

   269→### 3.2 Core methods
   270→
   271→```rust
   272→impl LayerUnit {
   273→    // --- Creation ---
   274→    pub fn new(doc: Layer, config: LayerConfig) -> Self;
   275→    pub fn new_empty(config: LayerConfig) -> Self;
   276→    pub fn from_snapshot(snapshot: &[u8], config: LayerConfig) -> Result<Self>;
   277→
   278→    // --- Authorization ---
   279→    /// Can we accept a write from this DID?
   280→    pub fn can_accept_write_from(&self, did: &str) -> bool {
   281→        self.subscribers.get(did)
   282→            .map(|s| s.permit_capabilities.write)
   283→            .unwrap_or(false)
   284→    }
   285→
   286→    /// Can we push updates to this DID?
   287→    pub fn can_push_to(&self, did: &str) -> bool {
   288→        self.subscribers.get(did)
   289→            .map(|s| s.consent_token.is_some())
   290→            .unwrap_or(false)
   291→    }
   292→
   293→    /// Can WE write to this layer? (viewer side check)
   294→    pub fn can_local_write(&self) -> bool {
   295→        self.config.capabilities.write
   296→    }
   297→
   298→    // --- Subscriber management ---
   299→    pub fn add_subscriber(&mut self, did: String, capabilities: Capabilities, tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>);
   300→    pub fn remove_subscriber(&mut self, did: &str) -> Option<LayerSubscriber>;
   301→    pub fn set_consent(&mut self, did: &str, consent_token: String);
   302→    pub fn update_subscriber_vector(&mut self, did: &str, vector: Vec<u8>);
   303→
   304→    // --- CRDT operations ---
   305→    pub fn apply_update(&mut self, data: &[u8], from_did: Option<&str>) -> Result<()>;
   306→    pub fn export_snapshot(&self) -> Vec<u8>;
   307→    pub fn export_update_for(&self, did: &str) -> Vec<u8>;
   308→
   309→    // --- Broadcast ---
   310→    /// Broadcast to all subscribers with consent (exclude sender)
   311→    pub fn broadcast_to_subscribers(&self, exclude_did: Option<&str>);
   312→
   313→    // --- Lifecycle ---
   314→    pub fn touch(&mut self);                       // update last_accessed
   315→    pub fn is_cold(&self, threshold: Duration) -> bool;
   316→    pub fn freeze(&mut self) -> Vec<u8>;           // export + drop doc
   317→    pub fn has_subscribers(&self) -> bool;
   318→
   319→    // --- Dirty tracking ---

   325→### 3.3 What moves INTO LayerUnit (from Scribe/subscription/broadcast/apply)
   326→
   327→| Currently in | Method | Moves to LayerUnit |
   328→|---|---|---|
   329→| subscription.rs | `authorize_subscriber_for_layers()` | `add_subscriber()` |
   330→| subscription.rs | `send_initial_state_to_subscriber()` | `export_update_for()` |

   332→| loro_observer.rs | authorized_dids check in observer | `can_push_to()` in observer |
   333→| apply.rs | `create_layer_from_peer()` auth loop | removed (no eager auth) |
   334→| apply.rs | `update_sender_vector()` | `update_subscriber_vector()` |

   340→## Part 4: New Scribe (thin router)
   341→
   342→### 4.1 Simplified ScribeState
   343→
   344→```rust
   345→pub struct ScribeState {
   346→    pub page_id: String,
   347→    pub our_did: String,
   348→
   349→    // === Layer management ===
   350→    pub units: HashMap<String, LayerUnit>,
   351→
   352→    // === Connection registry (peer lifecycle) ===
   353→    pub connections: HashMap<String, ConnectionInfo>,  // did → connection
   354→
   355→    // === Page-level config (from page_access permit) ===
   356→    pub page_config: PageConfig,
   357→
   358→    // === Storage ===
   359→    pub layer_storage: LayerStorageRef,
   360→    pub vector_storage: PeerVectorStorageRef,
   361→    pub permit_issuer: Option<PermitIssuerRef>,
   362→
   363→    // === Sync ===
   364→    pub sync_config: Option<SyncConfig>,
   365→    pub sync_event_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<SyncEvent>>,
   366→
   367→    // === Observability ===
   368→    pub capture_tx: Option<broadcast::Sender<String>>,
   369→    pub page_update_subscribers: Arc<RwLock<Vec<mpsc::Sender<PageUpdate>>>>,

   371→
   372→/// Connection-level info (not per-layer)
   373→pub struct ConnectionInfo {
   374→    pub did: String,
   375→    pub device_id: String,
   376→    pub ephemeral_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<EphemeralOutbound>>,

   379→/// Page-level config from page_access permit
   380→pub struct PageConfig {

   386→
   387→What's REMOVED from ScribeState:
   388→- `subscribers: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<...>>>` → split into connections (Scribe) + per-layer subscribers (LayerUnit)
   389→- `our_permit` → page_config (page-level) + per-layer config in each LayerUnit
   390→- `pending_layer_authorizations` → gone
   391→- `pending_update_source` → handled within LayerUnit
   392→- `validation_handle` → passed to LayerUnit on creation
   393→
   394→### 4.2 Scribe message routing
   395→
   396→```rust
   397→// Before: 50+ lines of permission checks, auth, broadcast in each handler
   398→ScribeMessage::ApplyUpdate { layer_name, update, from_peer, .. } => {
   399→    let unit = self.ensure_warm(&layer_name)?;
   400→    unit.apply_update(&update, from_peer.as_deref())?;
   401→    // LayerUnit handles: permission check, CRDT merge, dirty marking
   402→    // LayerUnit's observer handles: broadcast to subscribers, UI notification
   403→}
   404→
   405→ScribeMessage::Subscribe { did, device_id, broadcast_tx, ephemeral_tx, page_access_permit, layer_permits } => {
   406→    // 1. Validate page_access_permit
   407→    // 2. Store connection info
   408→    state.connections.insert(did.clone(), ConnectionInfo { did, device_id, ephemeral_tx });
   409→
   410→    // 3. For each layer_permit: add subscriber to the LayerUnit
   411→    for (layer_name, permit) in layer_permits {
   412→        let unit = self.ensure_warm(&layer_name)?;
   413→        let capabilities = parse_capabilities(&permit);
   414→        unit.add_subscriber(did.clone(), capabilities, broadcast_tx.clone());
   415→        // Send initial state
   416→        let update = unit.export_update_for(&did);
   417→        broadcast_tx.send(BroadcastPayload { layer_name, update, .. });
   418→    }
   419→}
   420→```
   421→
   422→### 4.3 Lifecycle management
   423→
   424→```rust
   425→impl Scribe {
   426→    /// Load layer from storage if not in memory
   427→    fn ensure_warm(&mut self, layer_name: &str) -> Result<&mut LayerUnit> {
   428→        if self.state.units.contains_key(layer_name) {
   429→            let unit = self.state.units.get_mut(layer_name).unwrap();
   430→            unit.touch();
   431→            return Ok(unit);
   432→        }
   433→
   434→        // Load from storage
   435→        let snapshot = self.state.layer_storage.load_layer(layer_name)?;
   436→        let config = self.state.layer_storage.load_layer_config(layer_name)?;
   437→        let unit = match snapshot {
   438→            Some(data) => LayerUnit::from_snapshot(&data, config)?,
   439→            None => LayerUnit::new_empty(config),
   440→        };
   441→        self.state.units.insert(layer_name.to_string(), unit);
   442→        // Set up Loro observer
   443→        setup_layer_observer(&mut self.state, layer_name);
   444→        Ok(self.state.units.get_mut(layer_name).unwrap())
   445→    }
   446→
   447→    /// Evict cold layers (called periodically, e.g. every 60s)
   448→    fn evict_cold_layers(&mut self) {
   449→        let threshold = Duration::from_secs(300);
   450→        let cold: Vec<String> = self.state.units.iter()
   451→            .filter(|(_, u)| u.is_cold(threshold) && !u.has_subscribers())
   452→            .map(|(name, _)| name.clone())
   453→            .collect();
   454→
   455→        for name in cold {
   456→            if let Some(mut unit) = self.state.units.remove(&name) {
   457→                if let Some(snapshot) = unit.take_dirty_snapshot() {
   458→                    let _ = self.state.layer_storage.save_layer(&name, &snapshot);
   459→                }
   460→            }
   461→        }
   462→    }
   463→}
   464→```

   466→---
   467→
   468→## Part 5: Wire Protocol — Unified Layer Sync
   469→
   470→### 5.1 The single sync pattern
   471→
   472→Every layer sync follows the same pattern:
   473→
   474→```
   475→Sender → Receiver:  LayerSync { layer_name, data, permit }
   476→Receiver → Sender:  LayerConsent { layer_name, consent }
   477→```
   478→
   479→This replaces:
   480→- Initial state delivery (send_initial_state_to_subscriber)
   481→- LayerPermit message
   482→- LayerConsentGrant message
   483→- AuthorizeLayerSubscriber internal message
   484→- DistributeLayerPermits coordinator message
   485→
   486→### 5.2 New wire messages
   487→
   488→```rust
   489→/// Sent when establishing sync for a layer (initial + ongoing discovery)
   490→pub struct LayerSyncMsg {
   491→    pub request_id: String,
   492→    pub page_id: String,
   493→    pub layer_name: String,
   494→    pub data: Vec<u8>,           // snapshot or incremental update
   495→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   496→    pub permit: String,          // layer permit token
   497→}
   498→
   499→/// Response: receiver consents to bidirectional sync
   500→pub struct LayerConsentMsg {
   501→    pub request_id: String,
   502→    pub page_id: String,
   503→    pub layer_name: String,
   504→    pub consent: String,         // consent permit token
   505→}
   506→
   507→/// Ongoing updates (after initial LayerSync + Consent)
   508→pub struct LayerUpdateMsg {
   509→    pub page_id: String,
   510→    pub layer_name: String,
   511→    pub data: Vec<u8>,
   512→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   513→}
   514→```
   515→
   516→### 5.3 Flows
   517→
   518→**Initial connection:**
   519→```
   520→1. Handshake (page_access permit exchange — auth only)
   521→2. Node issues layer permits for all layers the peer should access
   522→3. For each layer:
   523→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   524→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   525→4. Both sides now have: data + authorization
   526→5. Ongoing: LayerUpdate messages (no permit needed)
   527→```
   528→
   529→**New app installed:**
   530→```
   531→1. Node creates app layer, issues layer permits to each peer
   532→2. For each peer:
   533→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data: app_code, permit: { read: true, write: false, sync: true } }
   534→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   535→```
   536→
   537→**Dynamic channel created:**
   538→```
   539→1. Owner creates "channels/did:key:alice/general/messages" locally
   540→2. Owner → Node: LayerUpdate (sync_target rule — no permit needed)
   541→3. Node detects dynamic schema match (grant: "open")
   542→4. Node issues layer permits to all peers with page_access
   543→5. For each peer:
   544→     Node → Peer:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   545→     Peer → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   546→```
   547→
   548→**DM (explicit grant):**
   549→```
   550→1. Creator creates "dms/did:key:alice/room1/messages"
   551→2. Creator → Node: LayerUpdate (sync_target)
   552→3. Creator calls add_layer_access(layer, "did:key:bob")
   553→4. Node issues layer permit for Bob only
   554→5. Node → Bob:  LayerSync { data, permit }
   555→   Bob → Node:  LayerConsent { consent }
   556→```
   557→
   558→### 5.4 Removed wire messages
   559→
   560→- `LayerPermitMsg` → merged into `LayerSyncMsg`
   561→- `LayerConsentGrantMsg` → replaced by `LayerConsentMsg`
   562→- `LayerConsentAckMsg` → no separate ack needed (consent IS the ack)
   563→- `DistributeLayerPermits` coordinator msg → coordinator sends `LayerSync` directly
   564→
   565→### 5.5 Sync target rule
   566→
   567→The viewer always syncs all its layers to its sync_target (the node) without needing a permit. The node is a trusted relay. The viewer's LayerUnit doesn't check `can_push_to(node)` — it pushes unconditionally.
   568→
   569→This is the ONE special case. Everything else goes through permit + consent.
   570→
   571→---
   572→
   573→## Part 6: Courier Changes
   574→
   575→### 6.1 PeerActor subscription flow
   576→
   577→```rust
   578→// Old: Subscribe with one page permit, then complex auth dance
   579→// New: Subscribe with page_access permit + batch of layer permits
   580→
   581→pub struct SubscriptionRequest {
   582→    pub page_id: String,

   590→- `DistributeLayerPermits` → replaced by direct `LayerSync` messages
   591→- `NewDynamicLayer` SyncEvent → simplified to trigger `LayerSync` to eligible peers

   599→- Keep only `on_layer_sync` (receive data + permit, issue consent back)

   603→
   604→## Part 7: Gurkha Changes
   605→
   606→### 7.1 New permit types
   607→
   608→```rust
   609→pub enum PermitType {
   610→    PageAccess,     // access to Scribe, presence, ephemeral
   611→    LayerPermit,    // per-layer capabilities
   612→    LayerConsent,   // authorization to push to receiver
   613→}
   614→
   615→pub struct Capabilities {

   617→    pub write: bool,

   620→

   626→

   634→
   635→- `GrantType::Role` → replaced by `DynamicGrant::Open`
   636→- `role_permissions: HashMap<String, LayerConfig>` → gone

   650→
   651→## Part 8: Butler Storage Changes
   652→
   653→### 8.1 Per-layer permit storage
   654→
   655→```rust
   656→// Old: one page permit per (page_id, did)
   657→store_page_permit(page_id, did, token)
   658→
   659→// New: layer permits per (page_id, layer_name, did)

   671→
   672→### 8.3 What's removed
   673→
   674→- `store_viewer_layer_consent` (old consent model)
   675→- `store_viewer_consent` (old batched consent)
   676→- Role-based permit issuance helpers
   677→
   678→---
   679→
   680→## Part 9: Implementation Phases
   681→
   682→### Phase 1: Rich LayerUnit (scribe only)
   683→
   684→**Goal**: Make LayerUnit self-contained. No external API changes.
   685→
   686→1. Add `subscribers`, `config`, `permit_token`, `last_accessed` to LayerUnit
   687→2. Add methods: `add_subscriber`, `remove_subscriber`, `can_accept_write_from`, `can_push_to`, `broadcast_to_subscribers`, `export_update_for`, `apply_update`
   688→3. Move subscriber VVs from `SubscriberInfo.vectors` into `LayerSubscriber.version_vector`
   689→4. Move broadcast logic from `broadcast.rs` into `LayerUnit::broadcast_to_subscribers()`
   690→5. Move observer authorization check to use `LayerUnit::can_push_to()`
   691→6. Remove `authorized_dids` HashSet
   692→7. Remove `pending_layer_authorizations`
   693→8. Remove `authorize_subscriber_for_layers()`
   694→9. Remove `AuthorizeLayerSubscriber` message handling (becomes no-op or log)
   695→10. Simplify Scribe message handlers to route to LayerUnit methods
   696→
   697→**Tests**: Rewrite unit tests in layer_unit/mod.rs. Integration tests should pass with same intent (layers sync correctly).
   698→
   699→### Phase 2: Per-layer permits + capabilities (gurkha + scribe)
   700→
   701→**Goal**: Replace role-based access with capability-based.
   702→
   703→1. Add `Capabilities` struct to gurkha
   704→2. Add `DynamicGrant::Open` / `DynamicGrant::Explicit` (replace `GrantType::Role`)
   705→3. Add `PermitType::LayerPermit` and `PermitType::LayerConsent`
   706→4. Remove `role_permissions` from `DynamicLayerSchema`
   707→5. Remove `relationship()` usage across codebase
   708→6. Update LayerUnit to parse capabilities from layer permit
   709→7. Update page.lua DSL (remove role definitions, use capability flags)
   710→8. Write new permit_template.json
   711→
   712→**Tests**: Update gurkha unit tests. Update integration tests for new permit format.
   713→
   714→### Phase 3: Unified wire protocol (courier + scribe)
   715→
   716→**Goal**: Layer + permit travel together. Consent replaces complex auth chain.
   717→
   718→1. Add `LayerSyncMsg` and `LayerConsentMsg` wire messages
   719→2. Update PeerActor subscription flow (page_access + layer permits batch)
   720→3. Implement `on_layer_sync` handler (receive data + permit, issue consent)
   721→4. Implement `on_layer_consent` handler (store consent in LayerUnit)
   722→5. Remove `LayerPermitMsg`, `LayerConsentGrantMsg`, `LayerConsentAckMsg`
   723→6. Simplify Coordinator (`DistributeLayerPermits` → direct LayerSync)
   724→7. Remove `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` for open grants (node sends LayerSync directly)
   725→8. Keep `SyncEvent::NewDynamicLayer` only for triggering LayerSync to eligible peers
   726→
   727→**Tests**: Rewrite integration tests (layer_sync.rs). Same intent: static channels sync, dynamic channels sync, viewer writes work, late joiner works.
   728→
   729→### Phase 4: Butler storage + lifecycle (butler + scribe)
   730→
   731→**Goal**: Per-layer permit storage. Cold/warm layer management.
   732→
   733→1. Add per-layer permit storage to Butler
   734→2. Add consent storage to Butler
   735→3. Implement `ensure_warm()` on Scribe
   736→4. Implement `evict_cold_layers()` periodic timer
   737→5. Update layer persistence to co-locate snapshot + permit
   738→6. Remove old page permit storage (or keep for migration)
   739→
   740→**Tests**: Storage unit tests. Lifecycle tests (eviction, reload).
   741→
   742→### Phase 5: page_id transparency + cleanup
   743→
   744→**Goal**: Apps never see page_id. Clean up dead code.
   745→
   746→1. Remove all `normalize_layer_name()` calls inside Scribe (bare names only)
   747→2. Add page_id prefix at PeerActor wire boundary only
   748→3. Strip page_id prefix at PeerActor receive boundary only
   749→4. Update Lua API (scribe:map, scribe:list, scribe:create_layer — no page_id)
   750→5. Remove app-level `page_id .. "/" .. layer_path` concatenation in channels.lua etc.
   751→6. Delete dead code: old consent templates, old authorization functions, etc.
   752→
   753→**Tests**: Update all sample apps. E2E tests.
   754→
   755→---
   756→
   757→## Verification
   758→
   759→After each phase, the following should work:
   760→
   761→```bash
   762→# Build
   763→cargo build -p scribe -p courier -p gurkha -p butler
   764→

   766→cargo test -p scribe

   768→
   769→# Integration tests (rewritten for new API)

   771→
   772→# E2E

   774→```
   775→
   776→Intent of each integration test:
   777→1. Static layer syncs owner → node → viewer
   778→2. Dynamic channel (open grant) syncs to all peers
   779→3. Dynamic channel — viewer can write back
   780→4. Dynamic channel — late joiner receives existing data

    51→impl PeerCapabilities {
    52→    /// Parse capabilities from a JSON object

    55→            relay: obj.get("relay").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),

    57→            accept_publish: obj
    58→                .get("accept_publish")
    59→                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
    60→                .unwrap_or(false),
    61→            manage_layer_access: obj
    62→                .get("manage_layer_access")
    63→                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())

    71→            "relay": self.relay,
    72→            "share": self.share,
    73→            "accept_publish": self.accept_publish,
    74→            "manage_layer_access": self.manage_layer_access
    75→        })
    76→    }

    80→#[derive(Debug)]

    88→/// Parse and validate `authorized_peers` fact value.
    89→///
    90→/// Semantics:
    91→/// - missing or null => role-based distribution (`None`)
    92→/// - array of DIDs   => explicit recipients (`Some(Vec<String>)`)
    93→pub fn parse_authorized_peers_fact(
    94→    value: Option<&serde_json::Value>,
    95→) -> PermitResult<Option<Vec<String>>> {
    96→    let Some(value) = value else {
    97→        return Ok(None);
    98→    };
    99→
   100→    if value.is_null() {
   101→        return Ok(None);
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    let arr = value.as_array().ok_or_else(|| {
   105→        PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   106→            "authorized_peers must be null or an array of DIDs".to_string(),
   107→        )
   108→    })?;
   109→
   110→    if arr.is_empty() {
   111→        return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   112→            "authorized_peers must be null for role-based distribution or a non-empty DID list"
   113→                .to_string(),
   114→        ));
   115→    }
   116→
   117→    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
   118→    let mut peers = Vec::new();
   119→    for entry in arr {
   120→        let did = entry
   121→            .as_str()
   122→            .ok_or_else(|| {
   123→                PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   124→                    "authorized_peers entries must be strings".to_string(),
   125→                )
   126→            })?
   127→            .trim();
   128→
   129→        if did.is_empty() {
   130→            return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   131→                "authorized_peers entries must be non-empty DIDs".to_string(),
   132→            ));
   133→        }
   134→
   135→        if !did.starts_with("did:") {
   136→            return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(format!(
   137→                "authorized_peers entry '{}' is not a DID",
   138→                did
   139→            )));
   140→        }
   141→
   142→        if seen.insert(did.to_string()) {
   143→            peers.push(did.to_string());
   144→        }
   145→    }
   146→
   147→    if peers.is_empty() {
   148→        return Err(PermitError::ValidationFailed(
   149→            "authorized_peers must contain at least one DID".to_string(),
   150→        ));
   151→    }
   152→
   153→    Ok(Some(peers))
   154→}

   160→            PermitError::ParsingFailed(msg) => write!(f, "Parsing failed: {}", msg),
   161→            PermitError::MissingField(msg) => write!(f, "Missing field: {}", msg),
   162→            PermitError::ValidationFailed(msg) => write!(f, "Validation failed: {}", msg),

   314→impl DelegationTemplate {
   315→    /// Convert template to permit facts JSON
   316→    ///
   317→    /// This creates the facts structure that will be embedded in the delegated token.
   318→    /// Role-agnostic: only includes capabilities and patterns, no role-based logic.
   319→    pub fn to_facts(&self) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {
   320→        let mut facts = serde_json::Map::new();
   321→
   322→        // Add token_type
   323→        facts.insert(
   324→            "token_type".to_string(),
   325→            serde_json::Value::String(self.token_type.clone()),
   326→        );
   327→
   328→        // Add peer_capabilities
   329→        facts.insert(
   330→            "peer_capabilities".to_string(),
   331→            self.peer_capabilities.to_json(),
   332→        );
   333→
   334→        // Add operations (required for delegation chain - e.g., add_pages permission)
   335→        if !self.operations.is_empty() {
   336→            let ops_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   337→                .operations
   338→                .iter()
   339→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), serde_json::Value::String(v.clone())))
   340→                .collect();
   341→            facts.insert(
   342→                "operations".to_string(),
   343→                serde_json::Value::Object(ops_json),
   344→            );
   345→        }
   346→
   347→        // Add auth_capabilities
   348→        if !self.auth_capabilities.is_empty() {
   349→            let auth_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   350→                .auth_capabilities
   351→                .iter()
   352→                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   353→                .collect();
   354→            facts.insert(
   355→                "auth_capabilities".to_string(),
   356→                serde_json::Value::Object(auth_json),
   357→            );
   358→        }
   359→
   360→        // Add layer_patterns
   361→        if !self.layer_patterns.is_empty() {
   362→            let patterns_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   363→                .layer_patterns
   364→                .iter()
   365→                .map(|(pattern, config)| {
   366→                    (
   367→                        pattern.clone(),
   368→                        serde_json::json!({
   369→                            "create": config.create,
   370→                            "sync": config.sync,
   371→                            "write": config.write
   372→                        }),
   373→                    )
   374→                })
   375→                .collect();
   376→            facts.insert(
   377→                "layer_patterns".to_string(),
   378→                serde_json::Value::Object(patterns_json),
   379→            );
   380→        }
   381→
   382→        // Add fixed layers
   383→        if !self.layers.is_empty() {
   384→            let layers_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   385→                .layers
   386→                .iter()
   387→                .map(|(name, config)| {
   388→                    let mut layer_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
   389→                    layer_obj.insert("sync".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.sync));
   390→                    layer_obj.insert("write".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(config.write));
   391→                    if let Some(ref t) = config.layer_type {
   392→                        layer_obj.insert("type".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(t.clone()));
   393→                    }
   394→                    (name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(layer_obj))
   395→                })
   396→                .collect();
   397→            facts.insert("layers".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(layers_json));
   398→        }
   399→
   400→        // Add relationship (for logging only)
   401→        if let Some(rel) = &self.relationship {
   402→            facts.insert(
   403→                "relationship".to_string(),
   404→                serde_json::Value::String(rel.clone()),
   405→            );
   406→        }
   407→
   408→        // Add issue_on (self-describing templates for what to issue on actions)
   409→        if !self.issue_on.is_empty() {
   410→            let issue_on_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   411→                .issue_on
   412→                .iter()
   413→                .map(|(action, template)| {
   414→                    (
   415→                        action.clone(),
   416→                        serde_json::Value::Object(template.to_facts()),
   417→                    )
   418→                })
   419→                .collect();
   420→            facts.insert(
   421→                "issue_on".to_string(),
   422→                serde_json::Value::Object(issue_on_json),
   423→            );
   424→        }
   425→
   426→        // Add presence configuration
   427→        if let Some(ref presence) = self.presence {
   428→            let mut presence_json = serde_json::Map::new();
   429→            presence_json.insert(
   430→                "visible".to_string(),
   431→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.visible),
   432→            );
   433→            presence_json.insert(
   434→                "can_see_others".to_string(),
   435→                serde_json::Value::Bool(presence.can_see_others),
   436→            );
   437→            if let Some(ref name) = presence.name {
   438→                presence_json.insert("name".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(name.clone()));
   439→            }
   440→            facts.insert(
   441→                "presence".to_string(),
   442→                serde_json::Value::Object(presence_json),
   443→            );
   444→        }
   445→
   446→        // Add ephemeral_funcs (allowed ephemeral function names)
   447→        if !self.ephemeral_funcs.is_empty() {
   448→            let funcs: Vec<serde_json::Value> = self
   449→                .ephemeral_funcs
   450→                .iter()
   451→                .map(|f| serde_json::Value::String(f.clone()))
   452→                .collect();
   453→            facts.insert(
   454→                "ephemeral_funcs".to_string(),
   455→                serde_json::Value::Array(funcs),
   456→            );
   457→        }
   458→
   459→        // Add dynamic_layer_schemas
   460→        if !self.dynamic_layer_schemas.is_empty() {
   461→            let schemas_json: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
   462→                .dynamic_layer_schemas
   463→                .iter()
   464→                .map(|(pattern, schema)| {
   465→                    (
   466→                        pattern.clone(),
   467→                        serde_json::to_value(schema).unwrap_or_default(),
   468→                    )
   469→                })
   470→                .collect();
   471→            facts.insert(
   472→                "dynamic_layer_schemas".to_string(),
   473→                serde_json::Value::Object(schemas_json),
   474→            );
   475→        }
   476→
   477→        // Add authorized_peers for layer authority templates.
   478→        // Missing/None means role-based distribution.
   479→        if self.token_type == "layer_authority" {
   480→            if let Some(peers) = &self.authorized_peers {
   481→                let values = peers
   482→                    .iter()
   483→                    .map(|did| serde_json::Value::String(did.clone()))
   484→                    .collect();
   485→                facts.insert(
   486→                    "authorized_peers".to_string(),
   487→                    serde_json::Value::Array(values),
   488→                );
   489→            }
   490→        }
   491→
   492→        facts
   493→    }
   494→}

   519→    /// Keys: "page_request", "share_link", etc.

   522→    proof_chain: Vec<String>,

   524→    sync_facts: SyncFacts,

   533→impl Permit {
   534→    /// Parse permit token and extract all domain information.
   535→    ///
   536→    /// Role-agnostic: extracts capabilities and patterns, not role labels.
   537→    pub fn from_token(token: &str) -> PermitResult<Self> {
   538→        use tracing::trace;
   539→
   540→        trace!("Parsing permit token (len={})", token.len());
   541→
   542→        // Parse permit token (uses ucan library internally)
   543→        let parsed = Ucan::try_from(token)
   544→            .map_err(|e| PermitError::ParsingFailed(format!("Permit parsing error: {}", e)))?;
   545→
   546→        trace!(
   547→            "JWT decoded - issuer: {}, audience: {}",
   548→            parsed.issuer(),
   549→            parsed.audience()
   550→        );
   551→
   552→        // Extract facts as raw JSON (source of truth)
   553→        let facts_ref = parsed
   554→            .facts()
   555→            .as_ref()
   556→            .ok_or_else(|| PermitError::MissingField("Permit facts not found".to_string()))?;
   557→
   558→        // Convert BTreeMap to serde_json::Value for deserialization
   559→        let facts_value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(facts_ref)
   560→            .map_err(|e| PermitError::ParsingFailed(format!("Facts conversion error: {}", e)))?;
   561→
   562→        // Deserialize structured facts via serde (replaces ~60 lines of manual parsing)
   563→        let parsed_facts: PermitFacts =
   564→            serde_json::from_value(facts_value.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
   565→
   566→        // Keep raw facts map for get_fact() lookups
   567→        let facts: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = facts_ref
   568→            .iter()
   569→            .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
   570→            .collect();
   571→
   572→        trace!(facts = ?facts.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(), "Facts extracted");
   573→
   574→        // Parse issue_on templates
   575→        let issue_on: HashMap<String, DelegationTemplate> = parsed_facts
   576→            .issue_on
   577→            .iter()
   578→            .filter_map(|(key, val)| {
   579→                Self::parse_delegation_template(key, val).map(|t| (key.clone(), t))
   580→            })
   581→            .collect();
   582→

   591→            layers: parsed_facts.layers,
   592→            layer_patterns: parsed_facts.layer_patterns,

   594→            proof_chain,
   595→            sync_facts: parsed_facts.sync,
   596→            presence: parsed_facts.presence,

   602→    /// Parse a DelegationTemplate from a JSON value
   603→    fn parse_delegation_template(
   604→        key: &str,
   605→        template_val: &serde_json::Value,
   606→    ) -> Option<DelegationTemplate> {
   607→        let template_obj = template_val.as_object()?;
   608→
   609→        // Extract token_type
   610→        let token_type = template_obj
   611→            .get("token_type")
   612→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   613→            .map(String::from)
   614→            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("delegated_{}", key));
   615→
   616→        // Extract peer_capabilities
   617→        let peer_capabilities = template_obj
   618→            .get("peer_capabilities")
   619→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   620→            .map(PeerCapabilities::from_json)
   621→            .unwrap_or_default();
   622→
   623→        // Extract layer_patterns
   624→        let mut layer_patterns = HashMap::new();
   625→        if let Some(patterns_obj) = template_obj
   626→            .get("layer_patterns")
   627→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   628→        {
   629→            for (pattern, config) in patterns_obj {
   630→                if let Some(config_obj) = config.as_object() {
   631→                    layer_patterns.insert(
   632→                        pattern.clone(),
   633→                        LayerPatternConfig {
   634→                            create: config_obj
   635→                                .get("create")
   636→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   637→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   638→                            sync: config_obj
   639→                                .get("sync")
   640→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   641→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   642→                            write: config_obj
   643→                                .get("write")
   644→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   645→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   646→                        },
   647→                    );
   648→                }
   649→            }
   650→        }
   651→
   652→        // Extract fixed layers
   653→        let mut layers = HashMap::new();
   654→        if let Some(layers_obj) = template_obj.get("layers").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   655→            for (layer_name, layer_val) in layers_obj {
   656→                if let Some(layer_obj) = layer_val.as_object() {
   657→                    layers.insert(
   658→                        layer_name.clone(),
   659→                        LayerConfig {
   660→                            sync: layer_obj
   661→                                .get("sync")
   662→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   663→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   664→                            write: layer_obj
   665→                                .get("write")
   666→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   667→                                .unwrap_or(false),
   668→                            layer_type: layer_obj
   669→                                .get("type")
   670→                                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   671→                                .map(String::from),
   672→                        },
   673→                    );
   674→                }
   675→            }
   676→        }
   677→
   678→        // Extract relationship (for logging only)
   679→        let relationship = template_obj
   680→            .get("relationship")
   681→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   682→            .map(String::from);
   683→
   684→        // Extract operations (e.g., add_pages, share_page)
   685→        let mut operations = HashMap::new();
   686→        if let Some(ops_obj) = template_obj.get("operations").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   687→            for (op_name, op_val) in ops_obj {
   688→                if let Some(op_str) = op_val.as_str() {
   689→                    operations.insert(op_name.clone(), op_str.to_string());
   690→                }
   691→            }
   692→        }
   693→
   694→        // Extract auth_capabilities (can_connect, sync_enabled, etc.)
   695→        let mut auth_capabilities = HashMap::new();
   696→        if let Some(auth_obj) = template_obj
   697→            .get("auth_capabilities")
   698→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   699→        {
   700→            for (cap_name, cap_val) in auth_obj {
   701→                auth_capabilities.insert(cap_name.clone(), cap_val.clone());
   702→            }
   703→        }
   704→
   705→        // Extract issue_on (recursive - templates for what to issue on actions)
   706→        let mut issue_on = HashMap::new();
   707→        if let Some(issue_on_obj) = template_obj.get("issue_on").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
   708→            for (action_key, nested_template_val) in issue_on_obj {
   709→                if let Some(nested_template) =
   710→                    Self::parse_delegation_template(action_key, nested_template_val)
   711→                {
   712→                    issue_on.insert(action_key.clone(), Box::new(nested_template));
   713→                }
   714→            }
   715→        }
   716→
   717→        // Extract presence configuration
   718→        let presence = template_obj
   719→            .get("presence")
   720→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   721→            .map(|p| PresenceConfig {
   722→                visible: p.get("visible").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
   723→                can_see_others: p
   724→                    .get("can_see_others")
   725→                    .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
   726→                    .unwrap_or(true),
   727→                name: p.get("name").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(String::from),
   728→            });
   729→
   730→        // Extract ephemeral_funcs
   731→        let ephemeral_funcs = template_obj
   732→            .get("ephemeral_funcs")
   733→            .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
   734→            .map(|arr| {
   735→                arr.iter()
   736→                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))
   737→                    .collect()
   738→            })
   739→            .unwrap_or_default();
   740→
   741→        // Extract dynamic_layer_schemas
   742→        let mut dynamic_layer_schemas = HashMap::new();
   743→        if let Some(schemas_obj) = template_obj
   744→            .get("dynamic_layer_schemas")
   745→            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
   746→        {
   747→            for (pattern, schema_val) in schemas_obj {
   748→                if let Ok(schema) = serde_json::from_value::<DynamicLayerSchema>(schema_val.clone())
   749→                {
   750→                    dynamic_layer_schemas.insert(pattern.clone(), schema);
   751→                }
   752→            }
   753→        }
   754→
   755→        let authorized_peers = parse_authorized_peers_fact(template_obj.get("authorized_peers"))
   756→            .ok()
   757→            .flatten();
   758→
   759→        Some(DelegationTemplate {
   760→            token_type,
   761→            peer_capabilities,
   762→            operations,
   763→            auth_capabilities,
   764→            layer_patterns,
   765→            layers,
   766→            relationship,
   767→            issue_on,
   768→            presence,
   769→            ephemeral_funcs,
   770→            dynamic_layer_schemas,
   771→            authorized_peers,
   772→        })
   773→    }

  1033→    /// Check if a layer should sync based on permit configuration
  1034→    ///
  1035→    /// **Context**: Used to filter out local-only layers (sync: false)
  1036→    /// **Checks**: Layer lookup in `layers` section - check `sync` flag
  1037→    /// **Returns**: true if layer should sync, false if local-only
  1038→    ///
  1039→    /// With fully-resolved permits, layer names in the permit are already
  1040→    /// expanded (e.g., "abc123/products" not "{page_id}/products").
  1041→    pub fn should_sync_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str, _our_did: &str) -> bool {
  1042→        // Check direct match
  1043→        if let Some(config) = self.layers.get(layer_name) {
  1044→            return config.sync;
  1045→        }
  1046→        // Check with page_id prefix (for bare names like "products")
  1047→        let full_name = format!("{}/{}", page_id, layer_name);
  1048→        if let Some(config) = self.layers.get(&full_name) {
  1049→            return config.sync;
  1050→        }
  1051→        // Default: sync
  1052→        true
  1053→    }

  1055→    /// Check if permit allows writing to a layer

  1057→    /// **Checks**: Layer lookup for write=true, then schema fallback for creator access
  1058→    ///
  1059→    /// With fully-resolved permits, accepts both bare names ("products")
  1060→    /// and full names ("abc123/products"). For dynamic layers, falls back
  1061→    /// to schema matching if the creator's DID is in the layer path.
  1062→    pub fn can_write_layer(&self, layer_name: &str, page_id: &str, our_did: &str) -> bool {
  1063→        // Direct match
  1064→        if let Some(config) = self.layers.get(layer_name) {

  1067→        // Try with page_id prefix

  1069→        if let Some(config) = self.layers.get(&full_name) {
  1070→            return config.write;

  1073→        if crate::decision::matches_creator_schema(self, layer_name, page_id, our_did, "write") {
  1074→            return true;
  1075→        }
  1076→        false
  1077→    }

  1117→// Pattern Expansion Helpers
  1118→
  1119→/// Strip `{page_id}/` prefix from an expanded layer name to get the bare name
  1120→///
  1121→/// **Context**: Scribe uses bare layer names (no page_id prefix).
  1122→/// Permit patterns like `{page_id}/products` expand to `{uuid}/products`.
  1123→/// This strips the prefix to get `products` for Scribe's layer map.
  1124→///
  1125→/// **Example**: `"abc123/products"` with page_id `"abc123"` → `"products"`
  1126→/// **Pass-through**: `"app:Shop"` (no prefix) → `"app:Shop"`
  1127→fn strip_page_prefix(expanded: &str, page_id: &str) -> String {
  1128→    let prefix = format!("{}/", page_id);
  1129→    expanded
  1130→        .strip_prefix(&prefix)
  1131→        .unwrap_or(expanded)
  1132→        .to_string()
  1133→}

  1135→/// Expand placeholders in a pattern
  1136→///
  1137→/// **Placeholders:**
  1138→/// - `{page_id}` → replaced with page_id
  1139→/// - `{aud}` → replaced with did
  1140→///
  1141→/// **Example:** `{page_id}/orders/{aud}` → `shop123/orders/did:key:abc`
  1142→pub fn expand_pattern(pattern: &str, page_id: &str, did: &str) -> String {
  1143→    pattern.replace("{page_id}", page_id).replace("{aud}", did)
  1144→}
  1145→
  1146→/// Resolve {page_id} placeholders in permit facts
  1147→///
  1148→/// Replaces {page_id} in layer keys at all levels (top-level and nested issue_on).
  1149→/// Also removes `layer_patterns` from facts (replaced by dynamic_layer_schemas).
  1150→pub fn resolve_page_id_in_facts(
  1151→    facts: &mut serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
  1152→    page_id: &str,
  1153→) {
  1154→    // Resolve top-level layers
  1155→    if let Some(layers) = facts.remove("layers") {
  1156→        if let Some(layers_obj) = layers.as_object() {
  1157→            let mut resolved = serde_json::Map::new();
  1158→            for (key, val) in layers_obj {
  1159→                let resolved_key = key.replace("{page_id}", page_id);
  1160→                resolved.insert(resolved_key, val.clone());
  1161→            }
  1162→            facts.insert("layers".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(resolved));
  1163→        }
  1164→    }
  1165→
  1166→    // Remove layer_patterns (replaced by dynamic_layer_schemas)
  1167→    facts.remove("layer_patterns");
  1168→
  1169→    // Recurse into issue_on templates
  1170→    if let Some(issue_on) = facts.remove("issue_on") {
  1171→        if let Some(issue_on_obj) = issue_on.as_object() {
  1172→            let mut resolved_issue_on = serde_json::Map::new();
  1173→            for (action, template_val) in issue_on_obj {
  1174→                if let Some(mut template_obj) = template_val.as_object().cloned() {
  1175→                    resolve_page_id_in_facts(&mut template_obj, page_id);
  1176→                    resolved_issue_on
  1177→                        .insert(action.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(template_obj));
  1178→                } else {
  1179→                    resolved_issue_on.insert(action.clone(), template_val.clone());
  1180→                }
  1181→            }
  1182→            facts.insert(
  1183→                "issue_on".to_string(),
  1184→                serde_json::Value::Object(resolved_issue_on),
  1185→            );
  1186→        }
  1187→    }
  1188→}
  1189→
  1190→/// Match a layer path against a dynamic layer schema pattern (issuance-side only)
  1191→///
  1192→/// Used at dynamic layer creation time to validate that the node has authority
  1193→/// to create a layer of this type.
  1194→///
  1195→/// **Pattern:** `{id}` matches any single path segment
  1196→///
  1197→/// **Examples:**
  1198→/// - `channels/announcements/messages` matches `channels/{id}/messages`
  1199→/// - `dms/uuid-123/messages` matches `dms/{id}/messages`
  1200→/// - `orders/uuid-456` matches `orders/{id}`
  1201→pub fn matches_schema_pattern(layer_path: &str, schema_pattern: &str) -> bool {
  1202→    let path_parts: Vec<&str> = layer_path.split('/').collect();
  1203→    let pattern_parts: Vec<&str> = schema_pattern.split('/').collect();
  1204→
  1205→    if path_parts.len() != pattern_parts.len() {
  1206→        return false;
  1207→    }
  1208→
  1209→    path_parts
  1210→        .iter()
  1211→        .zip(pattern_parts.iter())
  1212→        .all(|(path_seg, pat_seg)| *pat_seg == "{id}" || path_seg == pat_seg)
  1213→}
  1214→
  1215→/// Check access across a page permit + set of layer permits (two-tier model)
  1216→///
  1217→/// Convenience function that delegates to `decision::can_access_with_layer_permits`.
  1218→/// Checks if any permit in the set grants the requested access.
  1219→///
  1220→/// Access check = page permit layers ∪ all layer permit layers ∪ schema fallback
  1221→pub fn can_access_with_layer_permits(
  1222→    page_permit: &Permit,
  1223→    layer_permits: &[Permit],
  1224→    layer_name: &str,
  1225→    page_id: &str,
  1226→    did: &str,
  1227→) -> bool {
  1228→    crate::decision::can_access_with_layer_permits(
  1229→        page_permit,
  1230→        layer_permits,
  1231→        layer_name,
  1232→        page_id,
  1233→        did,
  1234→        "read",
  1235→    )
  1236→}
  1237→
  1238→/// Match layer name against pattern with path-segment wildcards
  1239→///
  1240→/// **Pattern:** `*` matches any single path segment (delimited by `/`)
  1241→///
  1242→/// **Examples:**
  1243→/// - `shop123/*/did:key:abc` matches `shop123/orders/did:key:abc`
  1244→/// - `shop123/*/*` matches `shop123/orders/did:key:abc`
  1245→/// - `shop123/*` does NOT match `shop123/orders/did:key:abc` (different segment count)
  1246→pub fn matches_wildcard(layer_name: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
  1247→    let layer_parts: Vec<&str> = layer_name.split('/').collect();
  1248→    let pattern_parts: Vec<&str> = pattern.split('/').collect();
  1249→
  1250→    if layer_parts.len() != pattern_parts.len() {
  1251→        return false;
  1252→    }
  1253→
  1254→    layer_parts
  1255→        .iter()
  1256→        .zip(pattern_parts.iter())
  1257→        .all(|(layer, pat)| *pat == "*" || layer == pat)
  1258→}

1→//! Permit Service - Stateless permit token operations
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides stateless functions for permit token generation and delegation.
     4→//! All functions take signing key bytes and return signed permits.
     5→//!
     6→//! Usage:
     7→//! ```ignore
     8→//! let secret_key: [u8; 32] = identity.secret_signing_key();
     9→//! let (token, cid) = gurkha::issue_one_time(&secret_key, "owner").await?;
    10→//! ```
    11→
    12→use crate::crypto;
    13→use crate::decision;
    14→use crate::errors::{ServiceError, ServiceResult};
    15→use crate::parser::Permit;
    16→use base64::{engine::general_purpose, Engine as _};
    17→use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
    18→use tracing::{info, instrument, trace};
    19→
    20→/// Issue a one-time connection token
    21→///
    22→/// Used for initial device pairing (QR codes, connection strings).
    23→/// Facts-only approach - relationship determines permissions.
    24→///
    25→/// # Arguments
    26→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
    27→/// * `relationship` - "owner", "node", "peer_user", or "peer_node"
    28→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes), fields(relationship = %relationship, token_type = "one_time"))]
    29→pub async fn issue_one_time(
    30→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
    31→    relationship: &str,
    32→) -> ServiceResult<(String, String)> {
    33→    trace!("Issuing one-time connection token");
    34→
    35→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
    36→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    37→
    38→    let decision = decision::decide_one_time_token(&verifying_key, relationship)?;
    39→    trace!("Token decision created");
    40→
    41→    let (token, cid) = crypto::sign_permit(signing_key_bytes, &decision).await?;
    42→
    43→    info!("One-time token generated: cid={}", cid);
    44→    Ok((token, cid))
    45→}
    46→
    47→/// Issue a peer connection token
    48→///
    49→/// Establishes bidirectional peer connection with signed permit.
    50→/// Facts-only approach - no domain needed, relationship determines permissions.
    51→///
    52→/// # Arguments
    53→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
    54→/// * `peer_pubkey` - Base64-encoded public key of the peer
    55→/// * `relationship` - "owner", "node", "peer_user", or "peer_node"
    56→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes, peer_pubkey), fields(relationship = %relationship, token_type = "peer_connection"))]
    57→pub async fn issue_peer_connection(
    58→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
    59→    peer_pubkey: &str,
    60→    relationship: &str,
    61→) -> ServiceResult<String> {
    62→    trace!("Issuing peer connection token");
    63→
    64→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
    65→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    66→
    67→    let decision = decision::decide_peer_connection(&verifying_key, peer_pubkey, relationship)?;
    68→
    69→    let (token, _cid) = crypto::sign_permit(signing_key_bytes, &decision).await?;
    70→
    71→    info!("Peer connection token generated");
    72→    Ok(token)
    73→}
    74→
    75→/// Issue a page viewer authentication token
    76→///
    77→/// Facts-only approach - no domain needed.
    78→///
    79→/// # Arguments
    80→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
    81→/// * `page_id` - Page identifier
    82→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes), fields(page_id = %page_id, token_type = "viewer_auth"))]
    83→pub async fn issue_page_viewer_auth(
    84→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
    85→    page_id: &str,
    86→) -> ServiceResult<String> {
    87→    trace!("Issuing page viewer authentication token");
    88→
    89→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);

   159→/// Unified page delegation
   160→///
   161→/// Delegates a page to any audience using a template key.
   162→/// Template key determines the delegation pattern (e.g., "node", "viewer", "page_request").
   163→///
   164→/// # Arguments
   165→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key
   166→/// * `delegator_token` - Token of the delegator (must have share_page capability)
   167→/// * `action` - The issue_on action to use (e.g., "node", "viewer", "page_request")
   168→/// * `audience_pubkey` - Public key of the delegatee
   169→///
   170→/// # Returns
   171→/// * `Ok((token_string, cid))` - The delegated token and its CID
   172→///
   173→/// # Self-Describing Permits
   174→/// Permit must have `issue_on.{action}` defining what to issue.
   175→/// No role-based lookup - the permit carries its own delegation template.
   176→pub async fn delegate_page(
   177→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
   178→    delegator_token: &str,
   179→    action: &str,
   180→    audience_pubkey: &str,
   181→) -> ServiceResult<(String, String)> {
   182→    let _signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
   183→
   184→    // Self-describing: permit must have issue_on.{action}
   185→    let template = decision::extract_issue_template(delegator_token, action)?;
   186→
   187→    let parsed_permit = Permit::from_token(delegator_token)?;
   188→
   189→    // Extract page ID from facts (new terminology)
   190→    let page_id = parsed_permit
   191→        .get_fact("page_id")
   192→        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   193→        .ok_or_else(|| {
   194→            ServiceError::InvalidPermit("Missing page_id in token facts".to_string())
   195→        })?
   196→        .to_string();
   197→
   198→    // Validate token has share_page permission (from facts.operations)
   199→    let has_share = parsed_permit
   200→        .get_fact("operations")
   201→        .and_then(|ops| ops.as_object())
   202→        .and_then(|ops| ops.get("share_page"))
   203→        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   204→        .map(|s| s == "allow")
   205→        .unwrap_or(false);
   206→
   207→    if !has_share {
   208→        return Err(ServiceError::ValidationError(
   209→            "Token does not have share_page permission".to_string(),
   210→        ));
   211→    }
   212→
   213→    // Create delegation decision
   214→    let delegation_decision = decision::decide_delegation(
   215→        &template,
   216→        &page_id,
   217→        "page",
   218→        audience_pubkey,
   219→    )?;
   220→
   221→    // Use builder to create token
   222→    let builder = crate::builder::GurkhaPermitBuilder::from_bytes(signing_key_bytes);
   223→    let (token, cid) = builder.build(delegation_decision.into()).await?;
   224→
   225→    Ok((token, cid))
   226→}

   396→/// Re-issue a permit with additional layers merged in
   397→///
   398→/// **Context**: Used for dynamic layer grants (channels, DMs, orders).
   399→/// Parses the existing permit, merges new layers into its layer map,
   400→/// and re-signs with the provided key.
   401→///
   402→/// **Preserves**: All existing facts, layers, operations, issue_on templates.
   403→/// **Adds**: New layers from `new_layers` parameter.
   404→///
   405→/// # Arguments
   406→/// * `signing_key_bytes` - 32-byte Ed25519 secret key (node's key)
   407→/// * `existing_permit` - Current permit token string
   408→/// * `audience` - Audience DID for the new permit
   409→/// * `new_layers` - Layers to add to the permit
   410→///
   411→/// # Returns
   412→/// * `Ok((token, cid))` - Re-issued permit with merged layers
   413→#[instrument(skip(signing_key_bytes, existing_permit, new_layers))]
   414→pub async fn reissue_permit_with_layers(
   415→    signing_key_bytes: &[u8; 32],
   416→    existing_permit: &str,
   417→    audience: &str,
   418→    new_layers: std::collections::HashMap<String, crate::parser::LayerConfig>,
   419→) -> ServiceResult<(String, String)> {
   420→    trace!("Re-issuing permit with {} new layers", new_layers.len());
   421→
   422→    let parsed = Permit::from_token(existing_permit)?;
   423→
   424→    // Start from existing facts
   425→    let mut facts = parsed.facts().clone();
   426→
   427→    // Merge new layers into existing layers
   428→    let mut layers_map = if let Some(layers_val) = facts.remove("layers") {
   429→        layers_val.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default()
   430→    } else {
   431→        serde_json::Map::new()
   432→    };
   433→
   434→    for (name, config) in &new_layers {
   435→        let mut layer_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
   436→        layer_obj.insert("sync".to_string(), serde_json::json!(config.sync));
   437→        layer_obj.insert("write".to_string(), serde_json::json!(config.write));
   438→        if let Some(ref t) = config.layer_type {
   439→            layer_obj.insert("type".to_string(), serde_json::json!(t));
   440→        }
   441→        layers_map.insert(name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(layer_obj));
   442→    }
   443→    facts.insert("layers".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Object(layers_map));
   444→
   445→    // Build new token with merged facts
   446→    let decision = crate::decision::TokenDecision {
   447→        audience: audience.to_string(),
   448→        capabilities: Vec::new(),
   449→        facts,
   450→        expiry: None,
   451→        proofs: parsed.proof_chain().to_vec(),
   452→        proof_tokens: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
   453→    };
   454→
   455→    let (token, cid) = crypto::sign_permit(signing_key_bytes, &decision).await?;
   456→
   457→    info!("Permit re-issued with {} new layers: cid={}", new_layers.len(), cid);
   458→    Ok((token, cid))
   459→}
